column135:
04/Jan/15 11:40 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;This is fixed by removing the deletion confirmation from [line 47 of the reading blurb](https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/1962/files#diff-659a009d345162aed7d04c3f01f09519L47)
in order to allow for AJAX deletion of History items in Issue 4209.

The other solution to this problem would be to require the user to click through a
second page confirming that they wanted to delete the History item. Requiring confirmation
to remove an item from your History is the definition of overkill, since no significant
data (i.e. the work itself) is deleted, and users frequently complain that it's too
hard or slow to delete multiple items... and no one *reads* our confirmation messages
anyway, as evidenced by how many users accidentally delete works. So it is my firm
belief that this is the better solution. And I would also argue that there is precedent:
we do not ask for confirmation when deleting comments from your inbox because, again,
no significant data (i.e. the comment itself) is deleted.

column137:
15/Dec/16 8:50 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;*Why this happened:*
We take away the input field after you choose a tag, and that confuses browsers. In some (e.g. Safari 10.0), focus would stay on the now-hidden input, so you couldn't _see_ where it was, which was confusing, but at least hitting Tab would put it on the next field. But other browsers would just freak out and lose focus entirely, and you'd start back at the top of the page -- super annoying if you're halfway through filling out a form.

This less-than-desirable behavior would happen in any place we limit how many items you can enter in an autocomplete field. 

*What will happen now:*
After you arrow down or click to select the synonym, focus will be on the × for removing the syn -- then you can hit Enter to remove the tag and type a different one, or hit Tab to move on to the next part of the form.

Another good place to test it would be the URL field on http://test.archiveofourown.org/external_works/new. Type a little something in the URL field, select something from the autocomplete suggestions, and focus should go to the × near the URL you selected.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4019
otwarchive v0.9.15.45

On occasion, previously wrangled tags lose their wrangling - they'll be wrangled into
a fandom, only to re-appear in the fandom's bin as unwrangled tags.

This has been observed for some time now. For a while wranglers believed that these
were draft tags that the users were deleting the works, and then re-posting; but it
seems like that might not be the case.

One example was a set of freeform tags on this work:
http://archiveofourown.org/works/1660016

The wrangler simultaneously wrangled 3 new freeform tags into the fandom Welcome to
Night Vale.  A couple days later, one of these tags was still wrangled into the fandom:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Oddly%20fluffy%20for%20Desert%20Bluffs/edit
admin tracking: Last updated by [wrangler] on 2014-05-20 12:41:59 -0400

The other 2 tags were unwrangled and no longer in the fandom, and do not show any sign
of ever being wrangled; their Last updated is the author of the work, as is the case
with all unwrangled tags:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Basically%20Kevin%20can%20feel%20it%20when%20Cecil%20has%20sex/edit
admin tracking: Last updated by [author] on 2014-05-19 19:22:41 -0400

Thus far this has only been observed with wrangled, unfilterable tags (tags put into
a fandom but not canonized or synned), with tags losing their wrangled fandom; there
are no known cases of canonized or synonym tags losing their canonization/synning.

column1: Fandom canonicals temporarily gain "Uncategorized Fandom" media type from syns
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4032
otwarchive v0.9.15.78

New fandoms that are created have the Media parent "Uncategorized Fandoms". When synning
a new fandom to an existing canonical, the synonym gains the canonical's Media parent
and loses the "Uncategorized Fandoms" Media parent.

Sometimes, after synning a new fandom tag, the canonical fandom tag gains the Media
parent "Uncategorized Fandoms" for a brief period of time (length unknown, observed
to be a few hours) before it is automatically removed by the archive without wrangler
intervention.

This is an uncommon occurrence; most new fandom tags are able to be synned directly
to the canonical without transferring the "Uncategorized Fandoms" Media parent.

As of right now, this is affecting Marvel Cinematic Universe
https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Marvel%20Cinematic%20Universe/edit
but it will likely self-resolve.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

v0.9.15.86

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in the required fields
# Press “Save Draft”
# Press “Save Draft”
# Press “Add Chapter”
# Fill in some chapter text
# Press “Save Draft”
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Drafts
# Open the draft you just created

h2. What happens

There is no “This work is a draft and has not been posted.” message at the top of the multi-chapter draft work like there is for single chapter drafts.

h2. What should happen

Expect to see a message at the top of the work saying "This work is a draft and has not been posted. The draft will be *scheduled for deletion* on [DATE]."

This message should only show up if the entire work is a draft. If the work is posted and only the currently viewed chapter is a draft, then the current “This chapter is a draft and hasn't been posted yet!“ message at the top of the chapter is sufficient.

Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4050
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in

0.9.15

This was linked to closed issue 3993, but that one was already DTB.

So here's the description from the pull req:

We had a problem where creating, posting, editing, and deleting chapters was a lot
messier than doing the same for works. Now they should be a lot more alike.

    Puts the "* Required information" notice on the chapter form inside the form (instead
of above it) so it's pretty and blue like the one on the work form. (Also changed the
wording from "Required fields" to "required information" to match.)
    Puts the asterisk next to "Chapter Text" so it's properly marked as required.
    For "Work Text" and "Chapter Text," the asterisk is outside the translation string
so there's no worry about it disappearing during the translation process.
    Title-cases some fields on the chapter form to better match the title-cased fields
on the work form.
    Removes the "Delete Chapter" and "Discard Draft" buttons from the chapter form
itself and places a single "Delete Chapter" link at the top of the Edit Chapter page,
which is where the delete option is when editing works.
    Updated the confirmation text for deleting chapters to say, "Are you sure you want
to delete this chapter? This will delete all comments on the chapter as well and cannot
be undone!"
    Edit chapter page says "Edit Chapter" and new chapter page says "Post New Chapter."
Both have the work title listed below. (The pages always had visible headings, but
now the text is more like the text for works.)
    Likewise, the new work page says "Post New Work." (The text was always there, but
now it's visible for consistency with the Edit Work page and the chapter pages.)
    Chapter preview page now says "Preview" on the top, much like works say "Preview."
    Preview page for chapters now has its buttons in a fieldset, just like the preview
page for works does.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

Merging commit:

column134:
19/Aug/14 3:24 PM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;Having stepped through the code, I found that the parser does actually let the characters
through, and they last appear in the logs as ActiveRecord sends them, intact, to MySQL.


But they never get stored in the database; a bit of research suggests that the problem
might lie with the encoding for the "content" column in MySQL. I intend to update my
version of MySQL to one which has the option for 4-byte characters to see if that actually
solves the problem before we go doing anything rash. But it's possible that the problem
may also require a Rails upgrade which is another kettle of fish.

https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.5/en/charset-unicode-sets.html)

column138:
02/Sep/14 4:00 AM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;I finally got it working and got my smiley faces on a local Linux machine using Chrome.

However, it involves a few potentially breaking changes on the Systems side. In a nutshell,
the problem stems from a combination of MySQL's UTF-8 support and the mysql2 gem we
use to connect to it. To fix it, we need to do the following:

1. Convert all our databases and at a minimum the content column in the chapters table
on each one to use utf8mb4 encoding and collations rather than the current utf8 (see
https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/mysql-utf8mb4 for instructions on how to do this)
2. Upgrade our mysql2 gem to a version greater than 0.3.13
3. Amend the database.yml to include the following (instead of the same with "utf8"):
  encoding: utf8mb4
  collation: utf8mb4_general_ci
4. Test that emoji are working and more to the point, that nothing unexpected is broken,
especially with regard to maximum field lengths.

This will need to be discussed and scheduled after the indexing problems are resolved
anyway.

Oh, sorry -- I didn't give enough detail here. For logged in users, the x changes the
user's "Turn off the banner showing on every page" preference to true, and when an
admin sets the banner to active, it goes through the preferences for every user and
changes "Turn off the banner showing on every page" to false so they'll see the banner.
(That's why it gives the rather odd message, "Setting banner back on for all users.
This may take a while.") So logged in users will see new banners.

However, logged out users and logged in admins don't have a preference, so we have
to do that some other way. We use a cookie, so it lasts for the entire browser session,
regardless of whether the banner changes. (I used the existing code and behavior here,
as you can probably guess.)

I should note that there's only one cookie, so if you click the x while you're logged
in as an admin, the banner will stay gone while you're logged out (and vice versa:
if you click the x while you're logged out, the banner will stay gone while you're
logged in as an admin).

column1: Fix indexing and cache expiration
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4078
We currently have problems with elasticsearch indexing and cache expiration, so we're
making a few changes:

- Instead of going directly to elasticsearch, all indexing requests will now be queued
and run on a periodic basis
- Cache expiration should happen after we get the response back from elasticsearch
- Stats updates should only send the stats data rather than the full work document

To test, we should make sure that changes do eventually go through to the search engine
and that caches get expired properly.

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a tag:
-a new work is posted with that tag
-a work with that tag is updated
-a work is edited to add the tag
-a chapter is added to a work with that tag
-a work with that tag is deleted
-a work with that tag is edited to remove the tag
-the tag gains or loses a synonym
-the tag gains or loses a subtag

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a user or pseud:
-the user posts a new work
-the user updates a work
-the user adds a chapter to a work
-the user deletes a work
-the user is added as an author to an existing work
-the user is removed as an author to an existing work
-the user orphans a work
-a work by the user is added to an anonymous or unrevealed collection
-a work by the user is removed from an anonymous or unrevealed collection
-a collection that includes a work by the user is changed to no longer be anonymous
or unrevealed

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a collection:
-a work is added to the collection
-a work in the collection is updated
-a chapter is added to a work in the collection
-a work is removed from the collection
-a work in the collection is deleted
-the collection stops being anonymous or unrevealed

✔ a new work is posted with that tag

✔ the user posts a new work
✔ the user adds a chapter to a work
✔ the user deletes a work
✔ the user is added as an author to an existing work
✔ the user is removed as an author to an existing work
✔ the user orphans a work
✔ a work by the user is added to an anonymous or unrevealed collection
✔ a work by the user is removed from an anonymous or unrevealed collection
✔ a collection that includes a work by the user is changed to no longer be anonymous
or unrevealed

Note: The count in the user menu updates quicker than the side bar or index

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a collection:
✔ a work is added to the collection
✔ a chapter is added to a work in the collection
✔ a work is removed from the collection
✔ a work in the collection is deleted
✔ the collection stops being anonymous or unrevealed

Note: The side bar count is quicker to update than the index count

16/Feb/18 10:38 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Maybe there was an update that decreased the load on the workers? (Or a configuration change?)

The code for removing a meta-tagging through the interface first calls Tag.remove_association asynchronously, and then when the meta-tagging is deleted it triggers an asynchronous call to Tag.remove_meta_filters. So if you have two meta-taggings being deleted with sufficient delay between the deletions, and the Resque utilities workers are very responsive (i.e. very few things on the queue, or a lot of workers), these steps get executed in the following order:

1. In the interface, remove Lowest Tag as a subtag of Middle Tag.
2. "Middle Tag".remove_association("Lowest Tag")
3. "Lowest Tag".remove_meta_filters("Middle Tag")
4. In the interface, remove Middle Tag as a subtag of Highest Tag.
5. "Highest Tag".remove_association("Middle Tag")
6. "Middle Tag".remove_meta_filters("Highest Tag")

That order ensures that when step 3 is executed, "Highest Tag" is still a meta-tag of "Middle Tag." So when dissociating "Lowest Tag" from "Middle Tag," it will correctly dissociate "Lowest Tag" from "Highest Tag" as well (deleting the associated filter-taggings, and updating the appropriate Elasticsearch indexes).

However, if step 3 occurs after step 5 instead, the association between "Middle Tag" and "Highest Tag" will be gone when step 3 is executed, and "Lowest Tag" will never be dissociated from "Highest Tag." This leaves an incorrect, invisible meta-tagging in place, as well as all of the filter-taggings associated with that meta-tagging (and because the Elasticsearch filter_ids are built from the filter-taggings, Elasticsearch also gets it wrong).

I simulated this by suspending the workers while I made the changes in the interface, then re-enabling them. With only one worker, suspending the worker will cause it to fail every time; with more than one worker, there's a slim chance that the sequence of steps would work out, but it's still very likely to fail. In theory, suspending the workers should behave similarly to when all of the workers for the utilities queue are busy with other tasks.

I can also simulate it without suspending the workers by performing the two meta-tagging changes in a single edit (editing the Middle Tag and checking the boxes to remove both "Highest Tag" and "Lowest Tag"), which seems to cause it to fail pretty consistently. But I'm only running two workers, so I don't know if that would work with more.

from the Edit Series page; the Edit Work page should be for editing the work, not messing
with the series.  Or, if we want to keep the button, it should be labeled something
clearer, like "Delete Series", and the dialogue box should say something like, "Do
you want to delete this series?  The individual works will not be deleted."

column1: Title attribute in blurbs confuses some screen readers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4120 What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.) otwarchive test-0.9.30.2 If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen: http://test.ao3.org/works http://test.ao3.org/bookmarks http://test.ao3.org/collections What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. Using certain versions of some screen readers (e.g. unknown version of NVDA, OS X 10.6.7 VoiceOver 3.4.0 (210.15)), attempt to access some of the links in the blurbs on the aforementioned pages. What is the expected output? What do you see instead? Some methods of accessing those links (e.g. using the Web Item rotor in VoiceOver) will give insufficient information because they read the text of the title attribute instead of the link text (e.g. it will say "title" instead of reading the work's title). You can test this by viewing the page source and confirming that the blurbs do not contain elements with the title attribute. For example, a title on a work blurb currently looks something like

Work Title by username

. After this change, the h4 part should just say

. You can also test it with a mouse by hovering over the various sections of the blurb. Tooltips should no longer appear. Elements in work blurbs that should no longer have a title attribute: - work title - fandom tags - summary - stats Elements in mystery/unrevealed work blurbs that should no longer have a title attribute: - work title - summary Elements in bookmark blurbs' user modules (notes, user entered tags, etc) that should no longer have a title attribute: - bookmaker's notes Elements in external work bookmarks that should no longer have a title attribute: - work title - fandom tags - summary - stats Elements in collection blurbs that should no longer have a title attribute: - collection title - date - moderator list

column135:
23/Apr/22 5:34 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Because of a minor error in the way that the cache key is set in {{comments/single_comment}}, comment caches are never expired even though they look like they have {{expires_in: 1.week}} set:

{code:ruby}      <% cache(key: "/v2/single_comment/#{single_comment.id}/#{single_comment.edited_at}/#{single_comment.updated_at}", expires_in: 1.week, skip_digest: true ) do %>{code}

[(source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/views/comments/_single_comment.html.erb#L17]
Because the cache key is passed as a keyword argument, and the cache function expects at least one non-keyword argument, all of the keywords are converted into a hash and passed as the first argument to {{cache}}, which is then converted into a key that looks something like this:

{noformat}ao3-v2-dev:views/comments/_single_comment:8234591ee9f225dc96ab3129de848d1f/localhost:3000/works/18?expires_in=604800&key=%252Fv2%252Fsingle_comment%252F370%252F%252F2021-06-17+20%253A50%253A44+UTC&skip_digest=true{noformat}

That key is then cached with no expiration. The only way the cache ever gets expired is if someone replies to the comment, someone edits the comment, or memcached runs out of space and starts deleting old caches (which is extremely unlikely, because production has oodles of extra memcached space).

Obviously fixing that wouldn’t completely address this issue, because it’d still be good to have the name update immediately instead of in a week, but if the expiration were working and the problem fixed itself in a week, it might help cut down on the complaints.

Now that [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6333|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6333|smart-link] is in, there’s no extra loads required to get the user associated with the comment, which means that we can add {{user.updated_at}} to the comment cache key with very little overhead. This would ensure that the comment would expire whenever the user is touched, with no need for extra callbacks. column1: Potential match progress indication crashes when there are more than 1000 signups
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4136
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)



If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Find a challenge with (substantially -- at least 100-200 or else you'll probably
miss it) more than 1000 signups
2. Run potential matching
3. Reload the potential matching page and watch the progress indicator tick along
4. After the potential matching passes the 1000th signup, try to reload the potential
matching page
5. You get a 500 error

The progress indicator is the only part that's broken -- potential matching is actually
continuing on in the background. The issue is with this code in potential_match.rb:

    unless REDIS_GENERAL.exists(collection_byline_key)
      score = 0
      collection.signups.pseud_only.find_each do |pseud|
        REDIS_GENERAL.zadd collection_byline_key, score, pseud.byline
        score += 1
      end
    end

This code populates the "collection_byline_key" set with the pseuds of every user who
has signed up, which enables a progress indicator to be calculated by finding the rank
of the current user being processed inside the set. 

find_each is supposed to go through all the items in batches of 1000 (to avoid excessive
memory usage), but for some reason it is only doing one batch. As a result, this code
only puts 1000 names into the bylines list, and when we look for the rank of name 1001+,
redis doesn't find it in the list, so it returns nil and nil/1000 causes the 500 error.

The fix for this is to replace "find_each" with just "each". 

A temporary workaround is to just wait for the potential matching to complete (the
collection owners will be emailed when this happens), or if the progress indicator
is really needed, a senior coder can fix the collection bylines list in the production
console by running this small block of code:

collection = Collection.find_by_name(COLLECTION NAME GOES HERE)
collection_byline_key = PotentialMatch.byline_key(collection)
score = 0
collection.signups.pseud_only.each do |pseud|
  REDIS_GENERAL.zadd collection_byline_key, score, pseud.byline
  score += 1
end

column1: Prevent English news posts from being accidentally overwritten by translations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4144
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

v0.9.33.6.

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts

What steps will reproduce the problem?

1. Open English news post
2. Instead of creating a new news post for a translation, click on 'Edit' by mistake
3. Replace the English text with the translated text
4. Select the language and mark it as a translation

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Someone doing this by mistake would expect the translated news post to appear.
What actually happens is the English news post disappears; the existing post gets replaced
with a translation added to the latest news post (regardless of the original post having
been selected in the posting screen—that post disappeared, after all).
Any translations posted previously still remain linked to the original post, and clicking
on the link they show leads to the new translated overwritten version.
The overwritten post disappears from the news and tag listings.

When this happened, we tried to fix by replacing the post with the original English
content. We could select "English" as the language, but as we could not select for
it to be a translation of no post, it became listed as an English translation. The
mistake was finally fixed by using browser developer tools to manually re-add and select
the Please select option: <option value="" selected="selected">Please select</option>.


It would be good if there were a warning when one tried to overwrite a previously published
English post with a translation

01/Aug/19 10:42 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;* Logged out of the account I was logged into when this was deployed
* Logged in as admin
* Checked the admin page for that account and saw: 

|2019-08-02 01:21:31 -0400 (174.54.125.232)|Current Login|System Generated|
|2019-07-30 23:26:29 -0400 (174.54.125.232)|Previous Login|System Generated|

* Logged into that account on my phone using LTE so the IP would be different
* Refreshed the admin user page and saw:

|2019-08-02 01:29:35 -0400 (174.201.12.78)|Current Login|System Generated|
|2019-08-02 01:21:31 -0400 (174.54.125.232)|Previous Login|System Generated|

So the IP logging is correct. However, the IP address should *not* be in the first column (labeled “Date/Time”), but rather the third column (labeled “Details”), which currently says “System Generated.” “Details” is where we put, well, the specific details of an action, like “Old Username: sarken; New Username: sarking” when a user changes the name. 

I’d recommend consolidating this to one row, with the second column (“Action”) listed as simply “Login”, and the details reading “Current IP: 174.201.12.78; Previous IP: 174.54.125.232” or “Current IP: None recorded; Previous IP: None recorded” as needed.

I’d also recommend making this the top row, although that’s more subjective and less important than making sure the right information is in the right columns. I’m only suggesting it because I had a brief moment of thinking the code didn’t work when I had to scroll past all the really old account changes; it’s something we could certainly get used to having at the bottom.

column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4178
https://github.com/mperham/dalli
https://rubygems.org/gems/kgio

I decided to write Dalli after maintaining memcache-client for two years for a few
specific reasons:

The code is mostly old and gross. The bulk of the code is a single 1000 line .rb file.
It has a lot of options that are infrequently used which complicate the codebase.
The implementation has no single point to attach monitoring hooks.
Uses the old text protocol, which hurts raw performance.

So a few notes. Dalli:

uses the exact same algorithm to choose a server so existing memcached clusters with
TBs of data will work identically to memcache-client.
is approximately 20% faster than memcache-client (which itself was heavily optimized)
in Ruby 1.9.2.
contains explicit "chokepoint" methods which handle all requests; these can be hooked
into by monitoring tools (NewRelic, Rack::Bug, etc) to track memcached usage.
supports SASL for use in managed environments, e.g. Heroku.
provides proper failover with recovery and adjustable timeouts

Note to testers, there should be nothing to test.

the latter's function is browser-dependent.
* Browser support: IE handles feeds natively and automatically. Firefox can natively
support feeds as Live Bookmarks if enabled. Chrome and Opera do _not_ natively support
RSS without an extension. The current wording includes a verb, indicating action, but
at least two browsers don't do anything beyond load a page.
* Translation: "Subscribe" provides issues in translation, and will result in very
long buttons in some languages.

After discussion on Coders mailing list and discussion with Docs and Translators, a
simple label of "RSS Feed" will probably be the best, moving forward. We probably want
the orange icon as well.

When that bug was active, different unicorn workers could have ended up with different time zones, and the time zone that you saw would have been determined by which unicorn worker you got routed to. The {{updated_at}} value of the {{AdminSetting}} object is also [updated every time invitations are sent|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fcb6a8e6eeec7f5001d31da07d72219d82ee5ded/app/models/admin_setting.rb#L62]. Presumably that would happen in UTC, because the {{whenever}} schedule gets converted to a cron, and the servers use UTC for the system time. Not-so-coincidentally, 2014-12-30 01:21:21 -0500 works out to 6:21:21 AM UTC.

column135:
07/Jan/15 3:37 PM;557058:30a754c9-d9e6-464f-9f97-cb727ac8158f;First find all works posted in the last time period say a week.

Collect together the unique creators.

For each creator:
  count how many works they have created in the last say week.
  count how many works they have older than say a week.

Old works give a minus score, new works are a positive score

This would have a tendency to find new accounts which are posting lots of work.

We can change the score each work gives dependant on features of the work such as length
and say images inserted ?

I would only use this to guide humans at least in the first instance.

the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

v0.9.40.4

A banned user cannot post or edit works.  However, it's currently possible to add a
banned account as a co-author.  Doing so and then removing the posting user as an author
leaves the work attached only to the banned account, making it difficult to track down
the posting user.

from being suspened, so we'd like to make it impossible to add a banned user as a co-author.

6. Choose "Comments"

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect the comments to be arranged in order by chapter number.  Instead, the comments
are arranged by the _original_ chapter order.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

When viewing the work Chapter by Chapter, the comments are attached to the correct
chapters.

The comments correctly identify themselves as being on the correct chapter according
to the new ordering.

(Note that Issue 2406 means that the "Chapter X" title on both the chapter and the
comments does not necessarily change properly when chapters are re-ordered.  This seems
to resolve eventually on Beta, presumably when memcached runs out of memory, but doesn't
resolve on Staging over several days.)

The comment ordering does not seem to resolve on Beta even after several days.  Editing
the chapters and/or the work also does not seem to help.  The ordering is the same
logged in and logged out.

column134:
05/Jun/18 7:48 PM;557058:228562c8-74a0-4eb1-a336-9fb19937484d;So basically, the issue is that comments for the entire work mode are queried 'as is' - they are just extracted from the DB in whatever order it wants. I'm not sure how to solve this in an efficient manner - we can get the chapter new order using the position but then reordering the comments according to that seems somewhat inefficient to me.

column1: Homepage and Invite Requests page should indicate clearly when the invitation queue is turned off
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When an admin has disabled the automated invitation queue setting, the "Get Invited!" link is removed from the homepage and the form for requesting an invitation is removed from http://test.ao3.org/invite_requests. This leaves people confused about how to create an account, particularly because they sometimes enter their email address in the form for checking your position in the queue, which _is_ still on http://test.ao3.org/invite_requests.

*Therefore, we want to:*
* add a note to the homepage letting people know account creation requires an invitation, but invitation requests are disabled
* move the form for checking your invitation request status to a separate page, http://test.ao3.org/invite_requests/status
* make sure http://test.ao3.org/invite_requests is really, really clear about whether you can currently request invitations 
** and make sure both versions link to the page for checking your invitation status

We're also removing the "while we're in beta" references from the pages mentioned above, since it's entirely likely we'll use invitations even after we take the little "beta" off the logo when the whim strikes us.
  
*Testing notes:*
* Make sure checking your invite status works with JavaScript on and off, _and_ with an email address that is in the queue and one that isn't in the queue


----

Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4231
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

v0.9.44.0

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

http://archiveofourown.org/invite_requests

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

When "Invite from queue enabled (People can add themselves to the queue and invitations
are sent out automatically)" is not ticked (that is, the automated queue is turned
off) the Invite Requests page correctly doesn't have a box to add your email to the
queue.

However, it still has the "Wondering how long you'll have to wait?" box, which is labeled
"Email", and there is no message to say the queue is off.

This means that users coming from the FAQ (the Invite Requests page is linked from
both the Your Account and Invitations FAQ sections) see the box, enter their email,
hit "Look me up", and are confused by the message.

("Sorry, we can't find the email address you entered. If you had used it to join our
invite queue, it's possible that your invitation may have already been emailed to you;
please check your spam folder, as your spam filters may have placed it there.")

Ideally, when the "Add yourself to the list" box goes away, it would be replaced by
a message saying that the queue is off.

column1: Changing names of tags does not change the tag names on the work blurbs
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4239
When tag wranglers change the names of tags (either a wrangler changing capitalization
or diacritics, or wan admin swapping suffixes between tags) the tag names are very
slow to change on the works, and are not consistently changing on the work filters.

Tag name changes ARE working on Staging; this is only broken on Beta.  May be related
to Issue 4227.

On Beta, in the Testing fandom:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/works

The third work down is this one:
http://archiveofourown.org/works/3273401

Three days ago I renamed the tag "I am a test char" to "I AM A test char".  On the
work itself, that tag has updated (though it took a while, over 24 hours, I think?).
 But on the work blurb it still is appearing in the old form. (as far as I can tell,
this isn't a caching issue, as I posted a new work in Testing to refresh the works
cache, but the tag on the works still didn't update.)

For capitalization changes like this that's not as much of an issue (since it still
links to the same tag) but it's a problem when a tag is actually renamed by an admin
(mainly when we suffix-swap) since then the tag is effectively lost. E.g. this tag:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Coincidentally%20I%20am%20ALSO%20a%20test%20char%20-%20Renamed
still appears on the work as "coincidentally I am also a test char" - which now leads
to a 404 since a tag of that name doesn't actually exist.

What this does is clean up the reported URLs a tiny bit (http://archiveofourown.org/works/123
and http://archiveofourown.org/works/123?parameters=something both become http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/)
and then check if there were too many reports in the last month containing the same
"/works/123/" string (where "123" is the id of the reported work).

If works/123 already has 5 reports, it _will_ give an error for:
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123?parameters=something
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/chapters/456
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/chapters/456?parameters=something
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/chapters/456#anchor

If works/123 already has 5 reports, it will _not_ give an error for:
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123#anchor
http://archiveofourown.org/comments/show_comments?work_id=123
http://archiveofourown.org/chapters/456

Including a collection in the URL should not change the results: http://archiveofourown.org/collections/name/works/123/chapters/456?parameters=something
should still give and error and http://archiveofourown.org/collections/name/works/123#anchor
should still _not_ give an error


Works have /bookmarks, /collections, /comments, and /kudos pages:
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/bookmarks
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/collections
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/comments
http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/kudos

These will all count toward the 5 report maximum because they contain the string "works/123/".
If that's a problem, I can make adjustments, but I need to know which ones should not
count toward the maximum.

If it's important for http://archiveofourown.org/works/123#anchor to count toward the
5 report maximum, I can adjust that.

If it's important to keep the parameters on http://archiveofourown.org/works/123?parameters=something,
I can also adjust that.

If different chapters of the same work (e.g. http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/chapters/456
and http://archiveofourown.org/works/123/chapters/789) should not count toward the
5 report maximum, we can probably work something out.

Lastly, partial matches will not count toward the 5 reports, so if works/123 has 5
reports, you will still be able to report things like:
http://archiveofourown.org/works/1234
http://archiveofourown.org/external_works/123

column1: Story parser extracts spurious metadata from story text
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4267
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

0.9.54

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Import an external work which has a line starting with "Warning: <random ramble>"
in the middle of the story
2. Discover that the random ramble has been imported as a freeform tag because of the
fix for Issue 3732

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

In order to import from a variety of external sites like LiveJournal or people's personal
webpages, the story parser tries to scrape metadata from the raw HTML of the external
page by looking for lines starting with e.g. "Warning:", "Characters:", "Pairings:"
etc. Authors are particularly prone to inserting facetious warnings which will result
in false positives like this. The fix for Issue 3732 guards against actual warning
tags being created but still results in freeform tags being created instead. A similar
issue will occur with notes, which may create unwanted author notes if a story paragraph
begins with "Note:".

In the case where the external site is under our control (for OD mass imports), the
story parser needs to be amended not to parse the text it has identified as the chapter
content for metadata. This problem is not resolvable for other external sites as there
is usually no code-discernible distinction between the metadata and story text.

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Perform a mass import between a client web site and the Archive
2. Watch with horror as the Archive coughs up a 502, the client site times out, or
the Internet gods generally decide not to cooperate
3. Trawl through the imported works or use http://archiveofourown.org/redirect to work
out which individual works in the batch job were imported
4. Manually mark works as imported on the client site

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

The client side currently has to wait for a response from the Archive in order to work
out which works were imported successfully. If the connection between the two is lost
for whatever reason, the Archive may have imported all or some of the works anyway,
but the client will never know.

At the very minimum, there should be an end point that mimics the behaviour of http://test.archiveofourown.org/redirect,
and possibly a batch equivalent so the client can check the status of one or more works
based on their original URL.

26/Sep/15 8:34 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;I think the problem with 8 is the caching on the main bookmarks page, which is unchanged from production.

If you hide testy2's bookmark of "3883 for December 31 statistics" by testy, twofingerpost from http://test.ao3.org/bookmarks and then go to the bookmark itself at http://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/6784871 (which isn't cached), the bookmark has been successfully hidden even though the bookmark still appears on the heavily-cached main bookmarks page. 

The same is true for hiding a work -- if you hide a work that's on the main works page, it will still appear on the main works page with no indication it has been hidden. (I hid "Collection Uncategorized Fandoms Test" by sarken, which is still on the main works page, but which is hidden according to http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1061240 and also the "Your work has been hidden by the Abuse Team" email I received.)

column138: 26/Sep/15 8:48 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Okay, I took a look, and here's what's up: for http://test.ao3.org/bookmarks, everything is cached for ten minutes. That means if an admin hides a bookmark, it'll stay visible and the button text won't update, and if the user edits the bookmark to change a tag, add a note, or make it a rec, those changes won't show, either. The same is true with http://test.ao3.org/works -- if you edit your work while it's showing up there, the edits won't be visible, and if an admin hides a work while it's showing there, it will continue to show there.

column140: 27/Sep/15 2:18 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Right -- the bookmarks and works pages are cached so everyone gets the same version, which means anything with a restriction on who can see it won't show up on those pages. It might be time to rewrite the caching for those pages if it starts causing problems, but it's been that way since 2012. I think we haven't really run into any problems with it because we don't usually get to act on support and abuse tickets within ten minutes of the item being posted, assuming the item is one of the ones showing up on those pages (the caching means not everything will appear on those pages).

column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4276
What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive v0.9.55.2

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen: http://test.archiveofourown.org/locales
& http://test.archiveofourown.org/faq?language_id=en

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Log in with an admin account.
2. Access http://test.archiveofourown.org/locales and create a new locale.
3. Access http://test.archiveofourown.org/faq?language_id=en and try to access the
newly created locale with the language drop down to post a FAQ to it.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

You can't access the new locale, and it gives an error 500:

I18n.with_locale(Locale.find(66).iso)
  Locale Load (1.8ms)  SELECT `locales`.* FROM `locales` WHERE `locales`.`id` = 66
LIMIT 1
I18n::InvalidLocale: "da" is not a valid locale

(Replace "da" with your new locale ISO code.)

This is because the new locale is not in:

I18n.available_locales
 => [:en, :ar, :ca, :"zh-CN", :cs, :nl, :fi, :fr, :de, :he, :hu, :id, :it, :ja, :ko,
:lt, :pl, :"pt-BR", :ru, :es, :sv, :tr]

James says:

By default rails-i18n loads all locale files, pluralization and transliteration rules
available in the gem. This behaviour can be changed, if you specify in config/environments/*
the locales which have to be loaded via I18n.available_locales option:

config.i18n.available_locales = ['es-CO', :de]

rails-i18n README.md at 78d27afededa6cbfef1e801fafa4a00c3d746f1f · svenfuchs rails-i18n

https://github.com/svenfuchs/rails-i18n/blob/78d27afededa6cbfef1e801fafa4a00c3d746f1f/README.md

    I18n.config.enforce_available_locales = true
    I18n.config.available_locales = [:en, :ar, :ca, 'zh-CN', :cs, :nl, :fi, :fr, :de,
:he, :hu, :id,
      :it, :ja, :ko, :lt, :pl, 'pt-BR', :ru, :es, :sv, :tr]

in config/application.rb

I suspect that needs a I18n.config.enforce_available_locales = false

column142:
14/Aug/20 2:12 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;james_ and I ran {{bundle exec rake Tag:convert_non_canonical_warnings_to_freeforms}} on production.

In a couple cases, we had {{ArchiveWarning}} tags that could not be converted because a {{Freeform}} with the {{ - Freeform}} suffix already existed. This happened with {{ Wincest}} (note the leading space) and it was necessary to use the Rails console to replace the suffix’s dash with an em dash (making the converted tag {{Wincest – Freeform}}), per Tag Wrangling procedure. (If the em dash version already exists, Tag Wrangling’s next resort is an en dash.)

{code:ruby}User.current_user = Admin.find_by_login("admin-sarken")

aw = ArchiveWarning.where(name: " Wincest").first
 => #<ArchiveWarning id: 3751475, name: " Wincest", canonical: false, created_at: "2014-12-24 06:46:30", updated_at: "2014-12-24 06:46:30", taggings_count_cache: 1, adult: false, type: "ArchiveWarning", merger_id: nil, delta: false, last_wrangler_id: 82382, last_wrangler_type: "User", unwrangleable: false, sortable_name: " Wincest">

aw.name = "Wincest — Freeform"
 => "Wincest — Freeform"

aw.save
 => true{code}

Also in a few cases, we had tags that couldn’t be converted because the {{ArchiveWarning}} had a leading space _and_ there was a {{Freeform}}with the same name and no leading space. This happened with the warning {{ sexual situation}} (with leading space), since the freeform {{sexual situation}} (without leading space) already existed. In this case, we used the Rails console to add the regular {{- Freeform}} suffix to the warning tag before rerunning the rake task.

{code:ruby}User.current_user = Admin.find_by_login("admin-sarken")

aw = ArchiveWarning.where(name: " sexual situation").first
 => #<ArchiveWarning id: 4075415, name: " sexual situation", canonical: false, created_at: "2015-01-21 19:04:09", updated_at: "2015-01-21 19:04:09", taggings_count_cache: 0, adult: false, type: "ArchiveWarning", merger_id: nil, delta: false, last_wrangler_id: 126250, last_wrangler_type: "User", unwrangleable: false, sortable_name: " sexual situation"> 

aw.name = "sexual situation - Freeform"
 => "sexual situation - Freeform" 

aw.save
 => true {code}

What steps will reproduce the problem?

column1: Mass import URL checker should only search for exact matches
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4307
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

0.9.62

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Use the mass import API to import story A with the URL http://temporary.site/12345
-- it gets imported as http://ao3.org/789
2. Use the API import checking functionality to see whether story B with the URL http://temporary.site/123
has been imported yet
3. The Archive helpfully responds that story B is at http://ao3.org/789 - which is
actually where story A lives

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect to be told that story B hasn't been imported yet.

The API's URL checker uses the same method in the Work model as the redirect tool to
match an external URL to an AO3 work. Unfortunately, if it doesn't find an exact match,
the redirect tool performs increasingly fuzzy matching to account for end users importing
with query parameters etc. The final fallback is a partial match for any work whose
original URL *contains* the URL it is searching for. So "http://temporary.site/12345"
becomes a match for "http://temporary.site/123".

Since the API is only used by OpenDoors, we can assume that they will use consistent
URLs when importing and then searching for a URL. The API should only perform exact
matches. The redirect tool should remain as is.

* Going to the work navigation page and then coming back via a chapter link
* Going to the work endnotes from the first chapter while in chapter-by-chapter mode (side note: the url we’re directed to doesn’t have /works/id in it, just chapters/id. is that intentional?)

** Note: [+in full work mode leaving kudos appears to be broken (doesn't work at all) for people without javascript+|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5990], and there's a comment saying this can't be reproduced in local development so I'm not sure how we'd check whether the style param would lead to similar behavior
* Marking for later

* Using chapter index dropdown shown to users with javascript enabled
* Clicking "x more users" from the list of users who left kudos (probably not a problem? idk)

At this point I’m not really sure where to go next with this, but figured documenting these thoughts was a good start.

h2. Testing instructions

You need access to two accounts, including their emails, for this

# Log into an account whose emails you have access to
# In your preferences, pick a non-English locale that translates “Fandom” to a different word, e.g. Russian, Korean or Japanese
# Subscribe to two of your own works, ideally works with a few tags in a few categories. Note down which works you’re subscribing to
# Subscribe to yourself (on your own user dashboard)
# Log into a different account whose emails you have access to
# Make sure this account has a different locale set than the one from Step 2, e.g. English
# Subscribe to the two works from Step 3
# Log into the account from Step 1 again
# In quick succession, add one chapter each to the two works from Step 3
# Still in quick succession, post a work in an anonymous collection
# Wait for the subscription emails to arrive (or ask a friendly QA Supervisor to send them out early)
# Both users should receive one subscription email each, each email containing two chapters for two different works. The part of the email that lists the works’ tags should have the labels (e.g. “Fandom”) translated to the respective locale set in the user’s preferences. The rest of the email may remain in English. Make sure the emails have no errors or exposed HTML and that the subject makes sense. You should not get an email about the anonymous work that you posted

h2. Deploy notes

Mailer workers need to be restarted.

column1: External works with consecutive numbered URLs can't be imported in reverse order
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4325
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

0.9.63

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Use the mass import API to import story A with the URL http://temporary.site/12345
-- it gets imported as http://ao3.org/789
2. Use the mass import API to import story B with the URL http://temporary.site/123
-- but get the message that it has already been imported

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect story B to be imported. Unfortunately, this is a different manifestation of
the same problem as Issue 4307 - the existing URL checker resorts to increasingly fuzzy
matches when it can't find an exact match. So if one URL ends with "123" and one ends
with "12345", the one with "123" would need to be imported first because otherwise
it is seen as a partial match for "12345".

*Testing*

The problem is in the UrlFormatter, which is used by the following features:
- Redirect tool (http://archiveofourown.org/redirect)
- StoryParser (both the API and the manual import)

The API just calls the manual import code, so testing will involve importing two similar
URLs in the "wrong" order (eg: "12345" imported before "123") and then using the redirect
tool to check that both works can be found.

column1: Admins should be able to delete all things a spammer/troll created at once
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently when Abuse finds a spammer, they have to separately ban them and then delete all their works and other creations one at a time. This is bad. 

Instead: 
* when logged in as an admin
* on the manage user page in the warnings and notifications area, there should now be an additional option *Spammer: ban and destroy all creations*
* when selected, the following should happen:
** admin can enter custom notes if desired but if they don't, a default note about the user being banned for spamming will be inserted
** the user will be banned and the admin will get a confirmation page
** the confirmation page will list (paginated at 20 works & 20 comments per page) the user's works and comments for review. Bookmarks, series, and collections will also be available via links in the sidebar (the sidebar counts may be slightly inconsistent due to caching). 
** there should be a warning that all the creations will be destroyed and the action will not be reversible
* when the admin confirms, all the user's creations should be destroyed

column1: Mark works as spam/ham
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently works are submitted to Akismet for spam checks by the spam report, but there is no way to tell Akismet when they are getting it wrong, which is how Akismet learns to identify spam. 

We need to add a Mark As Spam/Mark Not Spam button to works for Admins which sends an update to Akismet. 

When logged in as an admin
And viewing a work
If the work is marked as "spam" by Akismet, there should be a button available in the options to mark it as not spam
If the work is not marked as spam or no response was recorded, there should be a button available in the options to mark it as spam
When the button is pressed the work's spam status should be updated

column1: Live search for fandoms and media pages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. [The All Fandoms Page|http://test.ao3.org/media]

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Enabled
1. There will be a "Search for fandoms" field with no submit button.
2. Enter two or more characters in the text field.
3. There will be a 500 millisecond delay after you last enter text in the field before the search begins.
4. A list of fandoms containing the text you entered will appear beneath a header specifying X Fandoms Found; the name of a fandom will link to the fandom's works page. If no results are found, no fandoms will be listed, but the 0 Fandoms Found header will appear.
5. The list will update when you add or remove text from the "Search for fandoms" field; when there are less than two characters in the field, the header and list will roll up and disappear.
6. When results have loaded, screen readers should tell you how many results have been found.

Note that the list of fandoms is cached for 4 hours for performance, so newly-canonized fandoms may not appear immediately.

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Disabled
1. There will be a "Search for fandoms" field with a "Search Fandoms" submit button.
2. The search field will behave like a [Tag Search|http://test.ao3.org/tags/search] where "Fandom" has been selected from the dropdown menu and "Canonical" has been checked. The page will reload and then display the results with the same as the JavaScript version ("X Fandoms Found" header, a list of fandom names that link to the fandoms' works pages).

h1. A Fandoms Page (Ex: [Movie Fandoms Page|http://test.ao3.org/media/Movies/fandoms])

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Enabled
1. There will be a "Search for fandoms" field with no submit button.
2. Enter two or more characters in the text field.
3. There will be a 500 millisecond delay after you last enter text in the field before the search begins.
4. A list of fandoms containing the text you entered will appear beneath a header specifying X Fandoms Found; the name of a fandom will link to the fandom's works page. If no results are found, no fandoms will be listed, but the 0 Fandoms Found header will appear.
5. The list will update when you add or remove text from the "Search for fandoms" field; when there are less than two characters in the field, the header and list will roll up and disappear.
6. When results have loaded, screen readers should tell you how many results have been found.

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Disabled
1. The page will be the same as it currently is, with instructions about in-page search but no search field: "You can search this page by pressing CTRL+F or CMD+F and entering what you are looking for." (It doesn't make much sense to build a new search function that will require a page reload when all possible results are already available in a neatly alphabetized list.)

h1. Other Notes
1. The behavior for fandoms pages will also exist on collections' fandoms page, e.g. [Yuletide's fandoms page|http://test.ao3.org/collections/yuletide/fandoms] or [Yuletide's Theater Fandoms page|http://test.ao3.org/collections/yuletide/fandoms?utf8=%E2%9C%93&medium_id=Theater&commit=Show]

https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Automated-Testing lists 9 tests which frequently but intermittently fail on our CI systems (Travis and Codeship). They all fail on the "And I should see..." step where Capybara tries to find new text on a page following an update or edit, but they only fail intermittently, which suggests that the pages may be loading too slowly or are sometimes -- but not always -- cached in the wrong state.

The code for this ticket will add a mechanism to disable Rails caching on selected Cucumber tests to increase the likelihood that the page is correctly updated before Capybara tries to find the element.

*Testing steps:* check that the test suite passes on Travis and Codeship.

column1: Use HTML5 doctype
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Our doctype is currently the XHTML doctype <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-strict.dtd">, which is officially ungodly levels of embarrassing, especially since we've been using HTML5 attributes for a while now.

We should change it to the HTML5 doctype <!DOCTYPE html>. It will be lovely to run our pages through https://validator.w3.org and see errors like _ Bad value article for attribute role on element li_ instead of _Line 65, Column 36: there is no attribute "role"_. Then we can think about allowing some HTML5 elements or attributes through the sanitizer for users.

To test, you'll probably want to click through a couple pages of the Archive (like a dashboard page, a works page with filters, a collection page, and a dashboard page with filters) in a number of our supported browsers and make sure there are no visible changes. IE9 and lower are the only browsers where there is truly a risk of that happening.

Because this information is used to set the revised_at field for works, we routinely lose time information about when creations were published, which causes them to be (eg) displayed out of order, especially in automated tests where they get published within seconds of each other. 

In order to fix this in a way that can be safely migrated, we will need to create a new DateTime field with a new name in chapters to replace published_at, change the code to use this new field, migrate the db, copy the existing published_at values to this new field (with 00:00:00 as the time for them all), and then after the deploy remove the old published_at field. GOOD TIMES!

column30: We added a new boolean column to works (moderated_commenting_enabled), but because it wasn't defined as a boolean field in our mapping, elasticsearch got an initial '0' or '1' value and defined it as a numeric field. Shortest term solution is simply not to send the field to elasticsearch at all, since we're not using it for search anyway.

Use only one declaration per property per ruleset
The CSS parser we use retains only one declaration for each property, meaning that rulesets like
      .my-class {
        background: -moz-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%, #2989d8 50%, #207cca 51%, #7db9e8 100%);
        background: -o-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca 51%,#7db9e8 100%);
        background: -webkit-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca 51%,#7db9e8 100%);

will have all but the last background declaration removed (so your gradient would only show up in WebKit browsers). To avoid losing declarations with repeated properties, split each one into its own ruleset, like so:
      .my-class { background: -moz-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%, #2989d8 50%, #207cca 51%, #7db9e8 100%); }
      .my-class { background: -o-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca 51%,#7db9e8 100%); }

Font and Font Family
Unfortunately, you cannot use the font shorthand in your CSS. All font properties have to be specified separately, e.g., font-size: 1.1em; font-weight: bold; font-family: Cambria, Constantia, Palatino, Georgia, serif;

In the font-family property, we allow you to specify any font with an alphanumeric name. You can (but don't have to) specify the name with single or double quotes around it, just make sure the quotes match. (e.g., 'Gill Sans' and "Gill Sans" are both fine; 'Gill Sans" won't work.) Keep in mind that a font has to be installed on the user's operating system to work. It's a good idea when specifying fonts to use fallbacks in case your first-choice font isn't available. See a set of web-safe fonts with fallbacks.

We cannot allow the @font-face attribute. Sorry! If you have an uncommon font that you want to use in a skin you would like to share, we suggest adding a comment in the skin's "Description" field with a pointer to a place for users to download the font themselves, and using web-safe fonts as fallbacks.

URLs
We allow external image URLs (specified as url('http://somesite.com/my_awesome_image.jpg')) in JPG, GIF, and PNG formats. Please note, however, that skins using external images will not be approved for public use.
Keywords
We allow all standard CSS keyword values (e.g., absolute, bottom, center, underline, etc.).
Numeric Values
You can specify numeric values up to two decimal places, either as percentages or in various units: 
cm, em, ex, in, mm, pc, pt, px

PS: we highly encourage learning about and using em, which lets you set things relative to the viewer's current font size! It will make your layouts much more flexible and responsive to different browser/font settings.

Colors
You can specify colors using hex values (eg, #000000 is black in hex) or with RGB or RGBA values (e.g., rgb(0,0,0) and rgba(0,0,0,0) both give you black). This may be safer since not all browsers will necessarily support all color names. However, color names are more readable and easier to remember, so we also allow color names. (We suggest you stick to the set of commonly-supported color names.)
Scale
You can specify scale (for the transform property) as scale(numeric value) where the numeric value can be specified up to two decimal places.

Comments
Comments are stripped from CSS.

If you are new to CSS, here are the basics:
A line of CSS code looks pretty much like this: selector {property: value;}

The selector is either the name of an HTML tag (like body or h1), or it can be an id or class that has been set on a tag. The property is what you want to change in the contents of that tag (for instance the font size), and the value is what you want to set it to.

Examples:

Inside the "body" tag, set the font size slightly larger than the baseline: body {font-size: 1.1em;}
Inside any tags with the id "header", set the background color to purple: #header {background-color: purple}
Inside any tags with the class "meta", make the text blink: (we do not advise this) .meta {font-style: blink}

column1: FAQ Search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Behaviour*
* The search looks for matches in the question headers and the answer texts.
* The search is scoped to the selected language. It’s not possible to search across languages.
* When the form is submitted, the Categories listing is replaced with the results for the search term.
* The results a list of questions that contain the search term (either in the question or in the answer part). They are displayed as one long list, removed from their parent categories. Therefor the Expand/Collapse buttons are hidden, since they serve no functionality here.
* When a search doesn’t yield any results, the Categories listing will stay, and a error banner will be shown, saying that there were no results for the search.
* As of right now, there is a blue banner saying the FAQs are being translated and if something is missing, the user should check the English FAQ (it's visible in the mockups). We would like to have a similar note later on, displayed when a user submits a search in a non-English language. It should say that if the user can't find something, to try search in English, since that will always be the most complete FAQ.
* We won’t offer Search on a Category page, like [http://archiveofourown.org/faq/contacting-the-staff?language_id=en]. But this might be a future addition, if we see a need for it.

column1: Mass import: Chapter content and metadata overrides work metadata
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Background*
The StoryParser which imports external works is designed to detect metadata in the external content. This metadata overrides any information provided in the mass import API request, and also processes the API metadata incorrectly in some scenarios.

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*
Scenario 1:
# Use the API to import a work with no metadata in the chapter contents
# Specify both the work's title and the titles of each chapter in the API request
# Discover that the Archive now has a work whose title is the title of the first chapter

Scenario 2:
# Use the API to import a work whose content includes incorrect metadata (or text that looks like metadata, like a paragraph that starts with "Pairing:") 
# Specify the correct metadata in the API request
# The Archive now has a work with a whole paragraph as its pairing

*What is the expected output?*
I would expect the metadata in the API request to override any information the StoryParser thinks it has found in the story itself.

The desired solution is for the content metadata to be used only if the related field isn't provided in the API request.
column133:
15/Dec/15 2:54 PM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;I have implemented the desired behaviour, so that the *title*, *summary*, *fandoms*, *warnings*, *characters*, *rating*, *relationships*, *categories *and *additional tags* on imported works are filled in with the following priority (highest to lowest):

1. Fields provided in the API request or Import Work form
2. Fields detected in the content, based on lines that start with *{{<field name>:}}* (this applies to everything except Categories, which wasn't implemented in the original version of the StoryParser, probably because external sites will usually use the word to mean what we call tags)
3. Default values ("Untitled Imported Work" for the work title, config-defined defaults for ratings, warnings and fandoms, and nil or empty for all the other fields)

*Testing*
Open Doors will check that the API works by checking that the temporary sites using it now import works correctly once this is on Test.

However, this change will also impact how manual imports work through the Import Work form, so it will be worth checking that the fields on the form do override anything the StoryParser might detect. For example:

1. create an html page on an external site with the following text (or use the copy at http://astele.co.uk/od-test/api-test-1.htm):

{code}
Title: I am a title
Summary: This is the summary
Rating: NC-17
Fandom: Star Trek
Pairing: Kirk/Spock
Characters: James T. Kirk, Spock
Tags: some freeform tags, and another one 

This is the story text.
{code}


2. Use the *Import Work* form on the Archive to import this external work, but tick the *Set the following tags on all works, overriding whatever the importer finds.* box and change the fields at the bottom of the form as follows:
+Rating:+ G
+Fandom:+ Harry Potter - J. K. Rowling
+Relationships:+ Draco Malfoy/Harry Potter
+Characters:+ Draco Malfoy, Harry Potter
+Additional Tags:+ some different freeform tags, and another different one 

3. The values in the latter should override the values in the former

4. Repeat step 1 with a different URL (or use the file at http://astele.co.uk/od-test/api-test-2.htm) and then import it without overriding the fields, and you should this time get the values that were in the original document.

column1: Store sortable name on subscription object
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In order to sort subscriptions by title/name, we currently get all subscriptions for a user in the subscriptions controller and then for each one, we go get the subscribed object in order to compare it to the user's other subscriptions. If a user has many subscriptions, then this page will perform very poorly and make a very large number of database calls.

In order to improve this, we could add a "sortable_name" field to subscriptions as we have on works and tags. Then we can do the sorting in the database and only retrieve the subscriptions that we need, as well as eliminating the extra n+1 queries to the subscribed works/series/users.

Challenges: there are a lot of subscriptions in the database, and we'd need to add a column to the table and then run a background rake task to populate it for existing subscriptions. Will probably take a while to run.

For the bug causing the subscriptions page to error if the user is subscribed to a deleted object but the subscription itself fails to delete, see AO3-4728.

column1: Translation: Make emails translatable and all the locales work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
All the bits and pieces required to make emails translatable. AO3 interface translation will be tackled after emails are translatable.

Emails are the first target for internationalization (i18n) because they have less edge cases than the AO3 interface. This will allow us to develop standards and workflows for i18n within a smaller scope. Once these standards are developed they can be used for the larger project of making the whole interface translatable.

Making an email translatable involves moving all strings to the locale ({{.yml}}) files by converting from {{ts()}} to {{t()}} according to the [i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards] and ensuring that the mails are sent with the locale set in the preferences by the user.

The locale preference for users is behind a rollout that can be enabled with {{$rollout.activate_user(:set_locale_preference, User.find(000))}} in the Rails console.

Ideally, translatable emails should have [mailer previews|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6776] to simplify testing the translated emails.

As the [i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards] have been largely established, the AO3 interface is now made translatable whenever it is touched during other work. However, email i18n is still the priority until the complete i18n workflow is more fleshed out, so tasks specific to the interface i18n (caching, handling of locale in URLs etc) are still under discussion.

column134:
10/Jan/16 4:28 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;According to https://github.com/rails/jquery-rails

>This gem provides:
>
> jQuery 1 and jQuery 2
> the jQuery UJS adapter
>assert_select_jquery to test jQuery responses in Ruby tests

However, we update our versions of jQuery and jQuery UJS by manually by replacing the files in `public/javascripts` (`rails.js` is our copy of `jquery-ujs.js`) and updating `app/views/layouts/_javascripts.html.erb`. So the only thing this will affect is our (already-broken) JavaScript tests.

If we _were_ to upgrade jQuery, we'd want to test... basically anything on the site that uses JavaScript. 

If we were to upgrade jQuery UJS, it would only apply to features that use the functions mentioned here: https://github.com/rails/jquery-ujs/wiki/Unobtrusive-scripting-support-for-jQuery That wouldn't include kudos, but it would include: 

- disabling a button after you click it (e.g. when the button on the posting form changes to "Please wait...")
- deleting anything that gives a confirmation pop up (e.g. deleting your history)
- some AJAX things that use data-remote: true (e.g. creating or editing bookmarks with the form that opens on the page)

column30:
First, get thee to the skin wizard:
1. Log in
2. Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins
3. Create Site Skin
4. Use Wizard

Or just go to http://test.ao3.org/skins/new?wizard=true

From there? Where to begin, where to begin...

1. The fields are all in one jumbled mess. Let's break them out into sensible chunks, e.g. a section for basic information, another for fonts, and another for colors.

2. Provide more information about the fields on the form instead of making users click the help text... but not by putting in in the label. For instance, instead of the field label saying, "Foreground color (name or hex code)," the label should be "Foreground color" and there should be a footnote-style message beneath the field telling users to format it as a name or hex code. If we use aria-describedby, it'll be read for screenreaders, too.

3. For clarity and accuracy, some labels should be changed. "Foreground color" label should be "Text color", "Font family" should be "Font", "Margin width" should be "Work margin width", and "Percent of base font size" should be "Percent of browser font size". The text on the skin's show page should match.

4. Entering a "Font" should do a better job of changing the font. Right now, for example, it fails to change the font on form buttons, e.g. Subscribe, Favorite Tag, or the font on the header's links. (Note: This can continue to change only the main font. Anything in Georgia, e.g. headings and the site name, should remain in Georgia. In the future, we can give users an ~accent font option for those.)

5. Entering a "Header color" should change the red parts of the header. Right now, it changes the white part. /o\

6. Entering an "Accent color" should change most of the grey parts, e.g. forms and the dropdown menus in the header. Right now it changes the dashboard, meta, and behind the icon in the header.

7. Entering a "Work margin width" should actually adjust the work margins in a fairly predictable way. Right now it really doesn't because of the max-width on the work area.

8. Entering a "Percent of browser font size" should increase or decrease all font sizes on the Archive by that percentage. Right now... idk. (This name is still a little misleading -- as you may know, most, but not all, of the Archive doesn't use your browser's font size, but rather a size that's ~87.5% of the default. Other name suggestions are appreciated.)

9. If a skin was created with the wizard, the edit link should drop you directly in the wizard.

10. If you create a skin with the wizard, you should also be able to add custom CSS to the same skin to override or tweak it, e.g. if you make the "Header color" a light pink and don't change anything else, you can choose "Edit," switch to "Write Custom CSS", and enter 
#header .heading a { color: purple }
to make the site name more readable on the white background. Right now, if you try to add custom CSS to a wizard skin, it completely overrides the wizard skin.

*Before this is deployed to staging,* make and apply a skin with the current incarnation of the wizard. This pull request includes an after task that will let you keep your existing wizard skin(s) as they now look. Why you'd _want_ to, I don't know, but...

column1: italics, justified, and The Clippening
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
when paragraphs of text are both italicised and justified, the rightmost edges of the text are cut off, presumably by the text’s margins/borders. 

From ticket conversation:

{quote} Basically, justified text runs in a straight line even with the right and left edges of the column/container, right? But when you apply italics, it slants the text right, effectively making it a couple pixels wider than normal.
 Normally, the browser will let those few tiny pixels visibly hang over the edge of the container (see normal_justified_italics.png). However, we apply overflow-x: auto; to the work container so when someone posts art that’s wider than the work area, the work area will scroll and show you the rest of the image. But the browser is also like, “Fuck it, I’m not making a scroll bar for a few pixels of text,” and that’s why the edge is getting cut off.
 We could trick it into showing those couple of pixels by adding some left and right padding (like 0.25-0.5em) to our workskin div{quote}
