column1: More margins
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Assuming you're using a browser default font size of 16px, go to a tag's works page (e.g. http://test.ao3.org/tags/Testng/tags) and resize your window to 992px to trigger the midsize or 672px to trigger the narrow layout. 

Notice there's a fairly dramatic shift in the size of the margins.

We'd like to increase the margins to get rid of or reduce that shift.

*There are a few pages that need their margins adjusted separately, so after confirming that the margins in the midsize and narrow views are generally bigger than they currently are on production, please also check:*
1) the inbox has the same margins as the rest of the site in regular, midsize, and narrow views (in regular view, the best way to check this is to look at your inbox and your works page -- there used to be bigger space between the dashboard & comments and comments & filters than there was between the dashboard & works and the works & filters, but now they should be the same)
2) the homepage has the same margins as the rest of the site in both midsize and narrow views
3) that work text has the same margin as the rest of the site in narrow view
4) that work text has slightly bigger margins that the rest of the site in the midsize view (it should be approximately the same as it is on production)


Some math to explain where the new 3.5% margins came from:

Assuming the user is used to browsing at 62em and they are using a default browser font size of 16px, their browser width is 992px. The margins are created by applying 2.5em of padding to the #main area, which has a font size of 0.875em, or 14px, making the margins 35px on either side (2.5 x 14). So in a 992px window, the margins each take up 3.5% of the page width.

But why assume they were used to browsing at 992px instead of, say, 800px, where the 35px margins would make up 4.3% of the page? Mostly because we're trying to keep the margins small, and because it will reduce the amount of jarring changes that happen as we go from normal to midsize to narrow.

column1: Remove time of day from draft deletion warning message, since it is a lie
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Drafts are deleted on the 30th day after they are created.  However, they are _not_ deleted exactly 30 days after the actual moment of creation; all drafts are deleted in a single task on that day.  This means that the times listed in the deletion messages are not correct.

When a work is previewed the first time the message is of the form:

"Draft was successfully created. It will be automatically deleted on Sun 13 Mar 2016 06:25PM PDT"

When a saved draft is accessed, it's:

"This work is a draft and has not been posted. The draft will be automatically deleted on Sun 13 Mar 2016 06:22PM PDT"

On the draft blurb:

"This draft will be automatically deleted on Sun 13 Mar 2016 06:22PM PDT"

All these should be changed to remove the time and leave only the date.

This block

{noformat}    if user.is_a?(User) && user.preference.time_zone
      # (snip)
      elsif !user.preference.time_zone
        user_time_string = link_to ts("(set timezone)"), user_preferences_path(user)
      end
    end{noformat}

seems like it wants to add a link to preferences when the user has not chosen a preferred timezone. However, it is conditioned on {{user.preference.time_zone}} being nil after verifying {{user.preference.time_zone}} is non-nil, which will mean "(set timezone)" is never added. Which seems like a bug?

I was tempted to just "fix" it by implementing what I think was the intention. However, that will probably mean a lot of users, who haven't touched timezone in preferences, will suddenly see "(set timezone)" appended after timestamps. Maybe the feature should be removed instead, or maybe there is a third way to resolve it. Perhaps there should be a separate Jira issue about this?

The solution to this issue is therefore to add the Notes field to the backend, the form and the API.

The *Delete Work* button is part of the sea of up to 12 grey buttons that appear at the top of works when viewed by the author. On mobile, it is quite easy to tap it by accident when aiming for the adjacent *Edit Work*, or *Chapter by Chapter* or *Entire Work*.

From Support:

column1: Assignment notification message in Collections settings doesn't keep line breaks
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Challenge / Collection maintainers can set a special message to be sent to their participants with their assignment.

To do this:

1) Log in.
2) Create a collection.
3) Access the Collection settings and make it a challenge 
4) Scroll down to the Profile section.
5) Enter the message, with line breaks (you can leave two line breaks -- that is, one empty line, between paragraphs, but it won't make a difference), into the "Assignment notification message" box. The box does warn about it being plain text.
6) Update the settings.

Set the challenge settings and get some sign ups, do matching and send out the assignments.

The assignments will include your text, but without any line breaks at all. That is at least somewhat inconvenient, as it can be wall-of-text-y depending on how much the mods write. The form also doesn't warn you line breaks won't work -- the field itself does keep the linebreaks, so it could be argued that the behavior when sending is unexpected.

Ideally, the line breaks would be kept when sending the message. If not, at least the form should clarify line breaks won't be kept.

If you use a screenreader to access the homepage, you'll notice three links that helpfully say only "Read more..." 

You _might_ be able to guess what you're reading more about if you're tabbing through all the links in order, but it would be much better if the link let you know by saying, "Read more... [Title of post]," as described in https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/ARIA7.html

The link text that is visible on the page will not change.

*To test in VoiceOver on Mac OS X El Capitan...*
1. Go to the Archive homepage
2. Press Command+F5 on your keyboard to launch VoiceOver
3. Select the Use VoiceOver option
4. Press the Tab key to go through the links on the homepage until you encounter a "Read more..." link, which should say, "Read more... [Title of post]"
5. Press Control+Option+U or Caps Lock+U to open the Rotor
6. Press the right or left arrow key until the Links menu comes up
7. Press the up or down arrow key to move through a list of all the links on the page and confirm that the "Read more..." links now say, "Read more... [Title of post]"

column1: Test wording of the archivist byline
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Following an incident in which Memcached got stuck and archivist bylines were not displayed correctly (original problem description below), we noticed that the automated tests for archivist imports didn't check for the correct byline. The original issue did not turn out to be a code problem, but the tests written while troubleshooting it are still useful.


----

Original problem description:
*Steps to reproduce the problem:*

1. Using an account which has archivist privileges, fill in the import work form 
2. Select the "Import for others" checkbox, enter any author name, and enter the email address of *an existing AO3 account*
3. Click Import.

*Incorrect behaviour*
At this point, the work will be posted with the archivist as the author. e.g.: a work imported by the archivist *testy* on behalf of Ariana will have the byline *by testy*.

*Expected behaviour*
Until recently (mid-February at least), the work would have been imported with the byline *by Ariana (ariana_paris)*. i.e.: the work should be transferred immediately to the user's account. This is occurring on Beta, but _doesn't_ happen on a local install or webdev. It _was_ also happening on Test, but a coincidental clear of memcached solved the problem, and all the works incorrectly associated with an archivist were then transferred to the correct accounts.

----

The problem was fixed by flushing memcache on Beta.
column133: 04/Apr/16 7:36 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;The original problem was due to memcached, but I've expanded a couple of tests to ensure we do notice if the code for the archivist byline ever breaks in future.

Support has asked us for a blacklist tool to prevent people from using certain email addresses to post guest comments. 

Current functionality (can also look at features/admins/admin_email_blacklist.feature for a hopefully readable set of tests): 

- When logged in as an admin can follow the "Blacklist" link in the header
- Can search for blacklisted emails or add new emails to the blacklist
- Emails will be "canonicalized" which means:
-- all lowercase
-- anything after a "+" in the username will be stripped
-- googlemail addresses will be converted to gmail

- Blacklisting a user's email should have no effect on their ability to post comments

column1: The dating system on works and chapters needs to be overhauled
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Per extensive discussion on Basecamp, now archived in the [Design: Work Dating Google Doc|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fGxNALWAqYfoFqRKXgnAiPVK0EAFOygcyejbQJQb2yA/edit?usp=sharing] (note: this is not a public document):

the dating system on works and chapters needs an overhaul. The plan is to move from our current system to the following simplified one:

* Works will have two DateTime fields, posted_at and changed_at
** posted_at will be the date the work was originally posted or imported to the archive
** changed_at will be the date the work was last significantly changed
*** significant updates include: chapter added, work posted or revealed
* Chapters will have one DateTime field, posted_at 
* All three of these fields will be user-editable and exposed in the main work and chapter forms
* The separate backdate setting will go away
* By default, Works will be listed in search results by the changed_at field 

This should fix the following bugs:

column1: Admin: Allow banner updates WITHOUT turning banner back on
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
1. Log in as admin
2. Banners > New Banner
3. Enter some Banner text
4. Select a Banner type
5. Check Active
6. Choose Create
7. In another browser, access the Archive as a guest or logged in user
8. Choose the × to dismiss the banner
9. In the window where you are logged in as an admin, choose the Edit option for the banner you created in steps 1-6
10. Change the Banner text or select a different Banner type
11. Choose Update Banner
12. As the guest or logged in user, refresh the Archive page you're on or navigate to another page
13. Be annoyed when you notice the banner is back

Sometimes an admin needs to update a banner without turning it back on -- for example, to correct a minor typo or to update the amount on a fundraising banner. This currently requires asking a database admin to update the banner text from the console, which is not a good use of anyone's time.

We want to add a checkbox to the banner form (for active banners only) that will allow admins to make minor updates to a currently-active banner without turning it back on and annoying our users.

column1: Allow for reordering of FAQ questions (not sections) and attach translations to the questions' anchors rather than position
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Admin users are currently unable to reorder FAQ questions within a section. 

This means that if a question has to be slotted in the middle of a section, a question has to be added at the end, and all questions' content moved down manually until the desired position is open for the new content.

Ideally, admin users would be able to re-order questions inside a section in a similar way they can reorder FAQ sections, or otherwise slot new questions in the middle of FAQs.

Other desired behavior for this improvement:
* Questions' translations would be attached to their question rather than the question's position, and so move with the question. (All translations / versions of a question could be attached to their 'anchor', for example.)
* Questions should only appear in translated versions of the FAQ section once they have been purposefully added to it (for translation). This would avoid English language questions that haven't been translated yet from appearing in the middle of translated sections.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Note: While it's possible to edit a work to have no fandom on both staging and production, staging does _not_ appear to give a 500 error. 

Here is the work I (as testy) was able to create the error with on production: http://archiveofourown.org/works/6485314

1. Log in
2. Post > New Work
3. Fill in the form
4. Post Without Preview
5. Edit Tags
6. Choose the "x" next to the fandom tag to remove it
7. Post Without Preview

You may or may not receive a 500 error immediately after posting. You will probably need to wait a few minutes for the error. It might not even work! Isn't this fun?

Regardless of whether the 500 error happens, however, you will _not_ be able to add a chapter to the work:

8. Add Chapter
9. Fill in the form
10. Post Without Preview
11. The new chapter form will just keep reloading without an error or success message, and the chapter count may increase to something odd like 2/1 with no new chapters visible on the work, e.g. http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1061566 (note that if you go to the Edit page for the work, you _can_ see the chapters listed above the form, so they're... sort of there, sort of not)

Ideally, we should make it so accessing a work without a fandom does not give a 500 error _and_ we should make sure you cannot save a work without a fandom by following the steps above. Just stopping the 500 error would be a big improvement, though.

Tracing the error points to trying to call the name method on nil in https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L223

column1: Language list not properly alphabetical
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
http://test.ao3.org/admin_posts
http://test.ao3.org/admin_posts/###

1. About > News
2. Open the select menu for Languages
3. Examine the list of languages in the menu
4. Look at a post with languages listed as Translations
 
Languages in the menu and on translated posts are currently sorted alphabetically by their short name, which means the list contains such seemingly inexplicable alphabetization as "Suomi" (fi) coming between "español" (es) and "Français" (fr). 

Much like we did with fandom tags, we want to add a sortable_name column to the languages table so admins can set an optional name to use for alphabetization. If no name is set, it should continue to fall back to the abbreviation (short_name).

That process should go like:

!Screen Shot 2016-04-20 at 10.38.30 PM.png|thumbnail! 

http://test.ao3.org/languages/ABBREVIATION/edit

1. Log in as admin
2. Go to languages page at http://test.ao3.org/languages
3. Choose "Edit" for a language, e.g. Suomi
4. Enter an optional name to sort on (e.g. Suomi) in a text field labeled "Name for alphabetical sorting"
5. Update Language
6. Voila ! Suomi is now with the other S-languages on the Language menu and in the list of translations on any news post that uses it

We want to do this via a new sortable_name column rather than using the languages' actual names to avoid having all the languages that begin with non-Latin characters ending up in a jumble at the end.

*Please note* that languages from http://test.ao3.org/languages are used in many places throughout the site. In addition to the admin post pages referred to above, here is a list of places that should be updated to use the sortable_name:

- http://test.ao3.org/works/search - work search page
- http://test.ao3.org/works/new - new work page (2 places: "Choose a language" dropdown in Associations section, and check "This work is a remix, a translation, a podfic, or was inspired by another work" option for a separate Language dropdown)
- http://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/works/edit_multiple - edit multiple works page
- http://test.ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works - filters for works listing
- http://test.ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/bookmarks - filters for bookmarks listing
- http://test.ao3.org/admin_posts/new - admin post form (needs admin access)
- https://test.ao3.org/languages - language list

Note: the following 2 locations are currently sorting by language name right now. This means that this fix will appear to "break" the alphabetical sorting on these pages until an admin adds sortable_names to the relevant languages.
- https://test.archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new - new abuse report
- https://test.archiveofourown.org/support - new support request

column1: Rename work posting buttons
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h3. The current situation
When you create an entirely new work, the options are currently:
Preview | Post Without Preview | Cancel
If you're working with an exisiting draft, another option is added:
Save Without Posting | Preview | Post Without Preview | Cancel
h3. The problem
The repetition of "Preview" and "Post[ing]" can cause unnecessary confusion over which button to choose. In the words of a user:
bq. Whenever I want to preview, I hesitate over which instance of "Preview" to click on, and twice now I’ve clicked on the wrong one, posted a work that wasn’t ready, and had to delete it. Plus my subscribers presumably got notified.
h3. The proposed solution
To eliminate this confusion, we can remove the overlapping words.
For an entirely new work, the options would be:
Preview | Post | Cancel
And for an existing draft, the options would be:
Save As Draft | Preview | Post | Cancel

column1: Works posted by a user fulfilling one of at least two open assignments that have the same recipient has all assignments checked by default on posting and editing form
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
This problem presents itself only if a user has two *open* (unfulfilled) assignments, both with the same recipient.

To test:

1. Get two challenge assignments on two different challenges with the same recipient.
2. Select the button to fulfill one of them.

The form will have both assignments checked (as if the work were fulfilling both), and both collections added. 

Unchecking one of the assignments allows the user to post properly fulfilling only one of the assignments. (Provided they notice.)

If the user doesn't notice the second checked box and posts the work fulfilling both assignments, the second assignment can be removed from the work by editing the work (edit the work, uncheck the unwanted assignment, remove the unwanted collection, post with or without preview).

As long as the second assignment stays open, the form defaults to checking both whenever the work is edited, forcing the user to keep unchecking the second assignment. 

The problem stops once there are posted works for both assignments, and posting the second work doesn't present the problem at all (because the first assignment is already fulfilled at the time).
column133:
12/Apr/18 6:10 PM;557058:045245cb-4c5b-4691-b41f-82c2b91416c7;Also, if you follow these steps you will also run into a variation of this bug:

1. Post a work fulfilling an assignment for Recipient A.
2. Receive another assignment, also for Recipient A (could be in another challenge).
3. Edit the first work, for instance to correct a typo.
4. Hit Post.
5. Work will now be marked as fulfilling both assignments, and be part of both challenge collections (and may become unrevealed/anon even if it was already revealed, depending on the settings of the second collection.)
column134:
03/Feb/19 10:23 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This happens as a result of the definition of the ChallengeAssignment comparison function (<=>), which only checks the bylines and doesn't look at the ID. And the {{include Comparable}} statement ensures that <=> is called when checking equality with ==.

So if two assignments have exactly the same offer_byline and request_byline, they're treated as being "equal" even if they're from different collections and have different IDs. (And this extends to when the view is trying to determine which checkboxes should be checked by default.)

One way to fix this would be to add on an extra comparison at the end involving IDs. However, I don't believe that comparison function is actually used to sort anything. (ChallengeAssignments generally seem to be sorted in the SQL query, not by calling sort. The function counts as covered according to codecov.io, but only because it's called when checking equality.) So a simpler alternative would be to just delete the comparison function and stop including Comparable.

column1: Potential match limitations not working leading to loss of mysql connection
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When potential match and assignment generation go on too long, the process can lose its mysql connection and cause the entire process to fail. In combination with a process that was restarting failed resque jobs automatically, this was leading challenges to restart matching endlessly until manually killed. (See http://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/Database_Admin_Things_-_AD%26T#Stopping_runaway_challenge_matching)

Potential matches are supposed to be limited to a max per challenge participant (currently 50), which has the effect of significantly speeding up matching because a great deal of time is spent generating unnecessary matches for participants who are highly flexible and can match many other individuals. These matches are then all compared against each other during assignment generation to select the "best" match, which further slows the process. 

The limit however never made it into cfengine and was therefore not being applied. In addition, while investigating this issue I realized that for a small collection, the absolute cap of 50 does not make much sense. Therefore, the cap has been changed to now be the smaller of 50 or 10% of the participants in a collection, with a floor on the cap of 10, in the case of very tiny collections (like the ones in our test suite). 

This new process has been manually used on a small challenge of 133 participants that was crashing repeatedly due to the lack of limits and produced successful results (3 people unassigned as giver, 3 as recipient, about as good as we expect to get for most challenges) while completing in literally one tenth of the time. 

The values POTENTIAL_MATCHES_MAX and POTENTIAL_MATCHES_PERCENT and POTENTIAL_MATCHES_MIN need to be added to cfengine.

column1: Inviting a work to an anonymous or unrevealed collection makes it anonymous or unrevealed
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Short version: invite a work to your anonymous or unrevealed collection and it will be anonymous or unrevealed, regardless of whether the creator has accepted your invitation.

Step-by-step version:
1. Log in as user1
2. Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in required information and check "This collection is unrevealed" or "This collection is anonymous" or both
4. Submit
5. Log out
6. Log in as user2
7. Hi, user2! > My Preferences
8. Uncheck "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."
9. Update
10. Post > New Work
11. Fill in required information
12. Post Without Preview
13. Log out
14. Log in as user1
15. Navigate to the work user2 just posted
16. Choose the "Add To Collections" button at the end of the work
17. Enter the name of your anonymous or unrevealed collection from earlier
18. Add

The work will now be unrevealed or anonymous, even though user2 has not accepted the invitation.

What should happen instead is the work should remain visible unless or until the creator accepts the invitation.

Marking high priority because it essentially allows anyone to hide a work, which has a fairly high potential for abuse. Fortunately, the creator can work around this by going to Hi, username! > My Collections > Manage Collected Works and choose the "Remove" option for the affected works. However, the work can still be re-invited (and thus re-anoned or re-hidden).

column1: Give certain admins the ability to remove pseud icons and update pseud descriptions
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Policy & Abuse needs the ability to remove pseud icons and update pseud descriptions. 

*Design/Testing*

* On [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds], admins with the policy_and_abuse or superadmin role should see the “Edit” link on the blurbs. Other admins should not see the link.
* They should be able to follow said “Edit” link to access the pseud edit page, [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds/PSEUD/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds/PSEUD/edit]. Other admins should not be able to access this page.
* Assuming there is an icon uploaded for the pseud, admins who can access the pseud edit page should be able to check the “Delete your icon and revert to our default” box and press “Update” to remove the icon. 
* Admins should also be able to modify the pseud description field.
* They should not be able to save changes to any other fields; ideally, the fields would be disabled.
* At the bottom of the edit form, there should be an "Ticket ID (required)" field that is only present for admins. It should have a footnote specifying only numbers should be entered, and it should be used to validate the ticket exists in Zoho, a la [AO3-6156|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6156].

When you save changes to the pseud:

If no number is provided, it should not save the change and should give the admin an error saying the field cannot be blank.

If a ticket with the number does not exist, the admin should not be able to save changes and should get an error message saying "Ticket ID must exist."

If a ticket with the number does exist, the change should be saved and a new admin activity log item should be created and displayed on the Activities admin page:

* the target should say "Pseud [name] ([user login])" and should link to the user's pseuds page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/LOGIN/pseuds}}), where you can see the descriptions and icons for each pseud
** if the pseud is deleted after the activity is created, it should say "Pseud [id]" and the link should point to {{/admin/activities}}, as it does for other deleted items
* the summary should say "Ticket #000 for User #000", and it should link to the relevant ticket on Zoho (we don't want to record a summary of the text before the change because pseud descriptions can include personal information subject to privacy laws; however, including the user ID number will give us some info to work with if the pseud is later deleted)
* the time of the change and the name of the admin who made the change should also be recorded

Note for testers: While on the Activities admin page, please also locate an activity for a destroyed work, follow the link, and check the summary. It should be an ugly bit of text like {{#<Work id: 123, expected_number_of_chapters: 2, created_at: "2023-06-15 05:21:55.000000000 +0000", updated_at: "2023-06-15 05:25:49.000000000 +0000", major_version: 2, minor_version: 0, [truncated for length, since you probably get the idea now]>}}.

*Notes*

This should be done using the [ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES_BY_ROLE|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/policies/user_policy.rb#L15-L22] approach we’ve implemented in the user and admin settings policies.

column1: No vertical space separating rows of buttons
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When a page on the Archive has many button-style links, the links may wrap onto multiple lines depending on the number of links and the width of your browser window. When this happens, there is no white space separating one row of links from the other, which is not only ugly, but also hard to use on touch screen devices.

We'd like to add some space between the rows.

Here are two places where it will be easy to see the problem, especially if you are on a phone (or shrink your browser window to something phone-sized, although this is _not_ a problem unique to the narrow stylesheet):
- Links at the top of a work, particularly if you own the work or are logged in as an admin: http://test.ao3.org/works/1062526/chapters/2127349
- Pagination links on a collection's work index: http://test.ao3.org/collections/yuletide/works
- Pagination links on a bookmark index: http://test.ao3.org/tags/Harry%20Potter%20-%20J*d*%20K*d*%20Rowling/bookmark

It will likely be important to look at a large number of pages on the Archive to make sure there are no unintended side effects.

column1: Can't use keyboard shortcuts to copy text from help pop-ups and other modals
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
http://test.ao3.org/works/search

1. Open a help pop up by clicking a ? near a field name
2. Highlight some text
3. Press Ctrl+C or Cmd+C on your keyboard to copy the text to your clipboard
4. In another window or in a text area, press Ctrl+V or Cmd+V on your keyboard to paste

*What happens...*

The text that gets pasted is _not_ the text you expect to have copied. Instead, it is what was already in your clipboard.

If you highlight some text, right-click (or equivalent) on it, and select Copy from the context menu that pops up, you will be able to successfully paste the expected text. 

You _can_ Ctrl+C/Cmd+C to copy text from a text box in a modal (e.g. the Share code on http://test.ao3.org/works/###).

*What _should_ happen...*

I _expect_ to be able to copy and paste whatever text I darn well please using my keyboard shortcuts.


*What poking the code has led me to believe*

This is related to the killing of events from outside the modal with !targetInModal: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/public/javascripts/ao3modal.js#L274 

It seems that the highlighted text on which you press Ctrl+C/Cmd+C does _not_ count as an event.target -- rather, the document is the event target, so targetInModal is set to false because the document has no parent element with the id #modal https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/public/javascripts/ao3modal.js#L267

29/Sep/16 5:09 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;There's a good chance that this is at least partly caused by caching issues. The updated_at field only has resolution down to the second, not the millisecond, so if two skin (or other) updates are performed within the same second, the cache key used to access the cached version of the data won't change between updates. But in order for caching to work properly (and always serve up the correct version of the data), the cache key has to change whenever the underlying data changes.

Long story short, if the tests run fast enough, the cache won't update properly, most likely leading to the two skin failures.

column1: Improve API error handling and roll over to v2
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The API was originally designed to mirror the behaviour of the existing StoryParser with minimal changes to the latter. Now that Open Doors are performing more semi-automated imports, the API needs better error-handling:

- the StoryParser currently throws a generic Error when anything goes wrong: it should return different errors depending on what happened
- similarly, the API relies on only a couple of HTTP status-inspired error codes and human-readable text messages to communicate errors - it should define a broader set of possible error codes and use the same ones for work and bookmark imports where appropriate
- it should not use HTTP statuses to communicate information beyond simple success/failure

The purpose of all this will be to allow API clients to take action automatically based on the errors, without breaking existing behaviour for manual imports.

*Testing*
Testing will involve checking that manual imports are unchanged, and API testing will happen using a mass import temporary site.

*ETA*: In order to implement this without breaking existing Open Doors import sites (about half a dozen already lined up), I am taking this opportunity to roll over the API version to v2 to accommodate the improved error codes and messages.

column1: Incompatible encodings: ASCII-8BIT and UTF-8 when importing
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When importing from external sites using either the manual importer or the API, some stories will fail with the message:

{quote}Encoding::CompatibilityError in WorksController#import
  incompatible character encodings: ASCII-8BIT and UTF-8{quote}

This is caused by non-ASCII characters like curly quotes or accented characters in metadata fields being passed around as raw data inside the story parser and choking upstream metadata processing.

This is a blocker for an ongoing import so will need to be deployed as soon as possible.

*Testing*:
Open Doors will provide a list of problem works on one of the temporary sites. If they import successfully, the problem will be fixed. This doesn't need archivist access.

column1: Download and Chapter Index menu positioning issues
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce/What happens

# Using a desktop browser, go to a multi-chapter work.
# If you're in Entire Work mode, choose "Chapter by Chapter" from the work navigation.
# Choose the Download option at the top of the work to open the menu.
# Choose the Chapter Index option at the top of the work to open the menu.
# Slowly decrease the width of your browser window, observing the behavior of the menus.
## At full width, assuming the navigation is all on the same line, the menus may overlap if they’re both open at the same time.
## As the screen gets narrower and the buttons wrap onto two lines, the menus may obscure the Download button, making it impossible to close the menu.
## Once the narrow stylesheet is triggered, the menus jump very high on the screen, overlapping the main navigation. If you just opened them at this width, you might not notice they opened because they’re so far removed from the buttons.
# Drag your window back to a wider width.
# Disable JavaScript in your browser. (This is no longer possible with Safari. It’s possible in Chrome, but in my experience, the message at the top of the screen sometimes disappears mid-resize, which slightly affects behavior, so Firefox works best.)
# Reload the page.
# Slowly decrease the width of your browser window, observing the behavior of the Download menu as you do. (The Chapter Index menu is not available when JavaScript is disabled.)
## It’s the same as 5a-c, but without JavaScript, it is always open.

h1. What should happen instead

h2. JavaScript enabled

The menus should always be positioned directly below the buttons that trigger them. While they may still overlap other buttons, you’ll always be able to close them to access those buttons.

h2. JavaScript disabled

With JavaScript disabled, the download menu should be displayed in a way that does not obscure other items on the page. (The Chapter Index menu will remain a link to the full page index.)

h3. Limitations

# With Javascript enabled, you will probably briefly see a flash of the non-JavaScript version when the page first loads. This is normal and happens currently, but it will probably be more noticeable with the new menu style.
# The menus may run partially off the edge of the screen if your screen is narrow and your font size is large. In the current version, this happens with the Chapter Index menu, but not the Download menu.
# If we ever want to add a button _after_ Download, it will look a little goofy because the button will move down below the open Download menu. 
# When JavaScript is disabled, the alignment of the Download header and buttons is slightly off, but it didn’t seem worth the code needed to fix a minor cosmetic issue. 

h1. Deploy notes

An admin will need to update the Reversi skin with the [latest Reversi CSS|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/public/stylesheets/masters/reversi/reversi_site_screen_.css]. 

Systems will need to run the recache skins playbook.

h1. Testing notes

Please repeat the “Steps to reproduce” using the Reversi, Low Vision Default, Snow Blue, and Dark Mode skins, which should all be in the footer. Please ensure the menus as well as the Chapter Index and Download buttons themselves have reasonable colors applied.

Additionally, please repeat them with a wizard skin that changes the background and accent colors and ensure they are applied to the menu:

# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin > Use Wizard
# Fill in the fields for Title, Background color, and Accent color
# Press “Submit” to save
# Press “Use” to apply 

Note that there is an existing bug in the Low Vision Default skin that makes the skin chooser buttons and true buttons (i.e., not links styled to look like buttons) in the work navigation turn into red text on a red background with a red border on hover or focus. ([AO3-7151|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7151]) This will apply to the Chapter Index and Download buttons now, since I have switched them from links to buttons.

I was having some trouble reproducing the second one last night, but I got it now. And now that I have seen it, I can say they’re the same problem, and it’s one I wasn’t sure whether to fix or not. (I’m going to use the Download button/menu as an example here, but it’s the same for both.) Basically, we indent all of our code to make it easier to work with, so the code for the download menu looks like this: {code:ruby} <% if downloadable? && AdminSetting.current.downloads_enabled? %>
    • <% ArchiveConfig.DOWNLOAD_FORMATS.each do |format| %>
    • <%= link_to ts(format.upcase), download_url_for_work(@work, format) %>
      • <% end %>
    • <% end %>{code} Which means the HTML looks like this: {code:html}
    • AZW3
    • EPUB
    • MOBI
    • PDF
    • HTML
    • {code} That results in a space before the button element (series of whitespace get collapsed into one space in HTML). And if you get your browser set to just the right width, that space – and therefore the start of the {{
  • }} -- can be on a different line than the button. When that happens, the menu factors that space into its positioning. So I can change the code to take away the space and leave a note to make sure no one fixes the incorrect indenting: {code:ruby} <%# The li, noscript, and button tags MUST be on the same line here to avoid the behavior described in https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4629?focusedCommentId=0000 %> <% if downloadable? && AdminSetting.current.downloads_enabled? %>
    • <% ArchiveConfig.DOWNLOAD_FORMATS.each do |format| %>
    • <%= link_to ts(format.upcase), download_url_for_work(@work, format) %>
      • <% end %>
    • <% end %>{code} That fixes the problem in Safari and Chrome, but leads to a worse issue in Firefox: if the Download button is on the second line by itself, the Download menu covers up the button. To fix that, I need to set the {{top}} positioning of the menu in the CSS, but that involves a [magic number|https://css-tricks.com/magic-numbers-in-css/] (i.e., a brittle bit of math that can break if something else changes): {code:css}.javascript .work.navigation .secondary { position: absolute; top: 1.911em; /* 0.375em * 2 for top and bottom padding + 1.286em for height + .25em to compensate for borders which are defined in pixels */ right: 0; align-items: center; gap: 0 0.643em; justify-content: space-evenly; }{code} So it’s fixable, but the quality of the fix is so bad I wasn’t sure if it was worth it. If the consensus after testing is that it’s necessary, I can definitely add it. (Hilariously, there’s another fix that would let us avoid this whole thing! But it’s brand new and only supported by the latest versions of Safari and Chrome – it’s not available in even the newest Firefox – so it’s not going to be a viable option for us for at least a few years.)

column1: Use relative paths for redirection
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Redirects should keep the protocol of the incoming requests, so users who need to use the insecure site (HTTP) don't get routed back to the main site (HTTPS). There are a few ways we can create absolute URLs in Rails: {{url_for}} by default, {{link_to}} by default, and {{_url}} route helpers. Note that {{redirect_to}} also uses absolute URLs by default, but we don't need to hunt for their uses because we rewrite redirects with nginx (to fix [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5945#icft=AO3-5945|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5945#icft=AO3-5945|smart-link]). Here is non-exhaustive list of places where we redirect to absolute URL from AO3-4995: As an admin: * Create an invitation for user specifying an email address * Invite a number of people from the queue * Give a user a number of invites * Delete an invitation * Delete a banner * Add an email to the list of banned emails addresses * Remove an email from the list of banned emails addresses * Delete an admin post * Delete an FAQ item * Delete a known issue * Delete a wrangling guideline * Reorder the invites As a user: * Delete the only chapter of a work * Delete a collection * Reject a gift * Delete a pseud * Clear your history * Logout As a guest: * Search and see if your invite is in the queue when it isn't * Add yourself to the invitation queue * Filter the list of collections This issue is particularly troublesome now because we occasionally end up redirecting users off the Archive and onto a proxy site. For example, a logged out user on {{https://archiveofourown.org}} attempted to filter the collection index ended up on {{http://ao3.tanioshizue.pw}} because the cache on one of our frontend servers had a version of the collection index page with the following HTML: {{

Filters

Filter collections:}}

A logged-in user who is _not_ the mod or owner of a prompt meme can still see the "Unposted Claims" page at [http://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION/claims|http://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION/claims] (zoho ticket 4614 has a live example). Specifically, each prompt contains

{quote}Request
by Anonymous claimed by FULFILLER_NAME{quote}

or 

{quote}Request

by REQUESTER_NAME claimed by FULFILLER_NAME{quote}

If you are not the mod and you attempt to access this page, you should be redirected to the collection with the usual permission error ("Sorry, you don't have permission to access the page you were trying to reach.")

Note that users still need to be able to access [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME/claims?for_user=true|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME/claims?for_user=true]

Logged out users who try to access this page are redirected to the log in screen.

*Testing instructions*

Verify you can access the page for your own claims in a collection you are not a maintainer of.

Verify you can access the page for your own claims in a collection you _are_ a maintainer of.

Verify you can access _all_ the claims in a collection you are a maintainer of.

Verify that you are not allowed to access all the claims in a collection you are not a maintainer of. *Note*: the generic “not allowed” message we have for collections is different from the one given above: "Sorry, you're not allowed to do that." (A bit “I can’t do that, Dave.”)

column1: Challenges: Speed up gift exchange matching
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We'd like to explore speeding up challenge matching through the following methods:

(1) Reduce SQL queries in ChallengeSignup.match and Prompt.match. (Challenge signups are bounded in size by limits set in ArchiveConfig, so it should be feasible to load the complete signup into memory, and avoid taxing the database with excessive queries.)

(2) It might be useful to process signups in small batches, to further reduce the load on the database.

(3) The current code reduces the set of signups to examine based on overlapping tags, and then runs ChallengeSignup.match on all candidate pairs of signups. But ChallengeSignup.match compares all of the prompts pairwise. For many exchanges, it might be faster to try to generate potential *prompt* matches through a similar overlapping-tag method, and then group up the potential prompt matches based on the offer signup id and request signup id (cutting down on the number of calls to Prompt.match).

column1: Mass Import: Add option to turn off metadata detection
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The StoryParser is designed to scrape metadata from the web pages it imports. However, this often results in rubbish tags being imported. Some specific problems have been addressed in AO3-4383 and AO3-3724 among others, but additional tags still scoop up rambling nonsense. In some cases, these are also invalid tags which make the import fail. 

When Open Doors are performing more semi-automated imports where the metadata is provided directly from the external site's database, there is no need to detect the metadata from the content - it's provided in the API call. There should therefore have an option to allow the detection to be turned off.
column133:
21/Sep/16 4:20 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;Following discussion with Support, AD&T and Open Doors staff about the overlap with the existing {{override_tags}}, we agreed on the following design for the options on the Import Work form:

Change the existing override_tags checkbox text to be as follows:

{code:none}
[ ] Set the following tags and/or notes on all works, overriding whatever the importer finds in the content.
    ( ) Use values extracted from the content for blank fields if possible
    ( ) Do no use values extracted from the content at all; use Archive defaults for blank fields
{code}

The radio buttons correspond to {{detect_tags = true}} (default) and {{detect_tags = false}} respectively. These should be greyed out or hidden in the import work form when the Override checkbox is not ticked (debatable though).

With the following behaviour:

*Checkbox UNTICKED {{override_tags = false}} - default*
All the fields are ignored. Tags are extracted from the content if possible, and defaults used for tags that aren't detected. 

*Checkbox TICKED {{override_tags=true}}*
- If a field is filled in, that value is used for the tag
- If a field is blank:
   if {{detect_tags = true}} is checked, then the value will be extracted from the content, or the Archive default used if there is no tag in the content
   if {{detect_tags = false}} is checked, then the Archive default for that field will be used

The API will work the same, except that {{detect_tags}} will be false by default as the API is used primarily for automated imports which provide the metadata from a database, so it never needs to detect work tags.

column1: Challenges: Assignment email has a warning as a rating
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

h2. Steps to reproduce:
1. Log in
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in required fields and choose "Gift Exchange" for "Type of challenge, if any"
4. Submit
5. On the form for setting up your gift exchange, check "Sign-up open?", enter 1 in the Allowed field for Rating and Archive Warnings for Requests, and leave the other defaults
6. Submit
7. Follow the "Sign-up Form" link in the sidebar
8. For the Requests, fill in Fandom with Testing and check "Graphic Depictions of Violence" as the Warning. For Offers, fill in Fandom with Testing.
9. Submit
10. Log out
11. Log in as a different user
12. Return to the collection page if necessary
13. Follow the "Sign-up Form" link in the sidebar
14. For the Requests, fill in Fandom with Testing and check "General Audiences" as the Rating. For Offers, fill in Fandom with Testing.
15. Log out
16. Log back in as the mod
17. Return to the collection page if necessary
18. Follow the "Challenge Settings" link in the sidebar
19. Uncheck "Sign-up open?"
20. Update
21. Follow "Matching" link in sidebar
22. Choose "Generate Potential Matches"
23. Choose "OK" on the random matches warning that pops up
24. Wait a few minutes
25. Refresh page to see potential matches
26. Choose "Send Assignments"
27. Choose "OK" on the confirmation warning that pops up

h2. What do you see:
In one of the assignment emails you receive, it will say only:

Fandom: Testing
Rating: General Audiences

In the other, it will say:

Fandom: Testing
Rating: Choose Not To Use Archive Warnings
Warnings: Graphic Depictions Of Violence

h2. The problem:
"Choose Not To Use Archive Warnings" is not a rating. Moreover, it's a little odd that Rating is included when no Rating was selected -- note how Warnings is not included when warnings are left blank.

h2. The solution:
One of two things should happen here:
1) Rating should be omitted from assignment emails if no rating is chosen. That would match the behavior with Warning.
2) If it is unacceptable to exclude the rating field, Rating should be "Not Rated" instead of "Choose Not To Use Archive Warnings"


h2. Notes:
For testing purposes, it was necessary to allow Rating and Archive Warning options for requests to:
a) determine wether the label (Rating) or the data (Choose Not To...) was wrong, and
b) ensure that the rating and warning fields otherwise work right

column1: Mass Import: Search existing works by title and author
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When Open Doors are preparing an external archive import, they must search manually for every work on the Archive to avoid importing duplicates where creators have already imported their own works. This is very time-consuming: the searching should be automated to provide a list of possible matches which can then be checked by human eyes.

Possible fields to match on would be: title, author pseud and fandom (or associated fandom). The full work blurb fields should be returned so the human checkers can decide whether that's the same work.

column1: Open Challenges page does not list open challenges in closed collections
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
[http://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges|http://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges]

1. Log in
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in the required "Collection name" and "Display title" fields
4. Check "This collection is closed"
5. Choose "Gift Exchange" for "Type of challenge, if any"
4. Submit
5. Check "Sign-up open?"
6. Fill in "Sign-up opens" with the current time
7. Fill in "Sign-up closes" with a future time
8. Submit
10. Browse > Collections > Open Challenges

I expect to see my challenge listed there, since sign ups are open. Instead, I do not. 

We currently exclude closed collections with open challenges from these listings: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/collection.rb#L187|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/collection.rb#L187] (not_closed refers to the collection status). 

It makes sense to remove this restriction because setting a collection to Closed until assignments go out is a logical step for a moderator to take in order to make sure all the works in the collection are related to requests/assignments/prompts.

*Update November 2025*: This issue was fixed as part of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6026|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6026|smart-link]. Converting this issue into removing the now unused {{signup_open}} method from Collection and adding an automated test to cover the behaviour here. No manual testing will be needed.

column1: Potential matches are not sorted by quality in autocomplete
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The autocomplete for potential matches (most easily visible on the potential matching pages on the No Recipient or No Giver tabs) currently lists the matches in random order. Since we now have quality in an easily accessible and not-db-intensive format, we would prefer to show the matches in sorted order, the same way they are assigned. 

To test this, check that the first potential match appears to be better than the last potential match. 

* Go to potential matching page and go to either No Recipients or No Givers tab
* Click in the empty text field and wait for the potential matches to pop up
* Look at the signups of the first and last potential matches and compare to the person being matched

Match quality is ranked by:

- number of prompts that match
- highest number of tags that match among the prompts

So you should expect to see the first potential match (at least for someone with a lot of options) be a person who has two prompts that match, or at least more tags that match.

column1: Unrevealed works can be downloaded
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
1. Log in
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in required fields
4. Check "This collection is unrevealed"
5. Submit
6. Follow "Post to Collection" link on the collection's page
7. Fill in required fields
8. Post

*What happens*
The work will have a "This work is part of an ongoing challenge and will be revealed soon!" banner at the top, but you'll be able to see the work and the download links because you're the creator.

Copy one of those download links and try it in another browser where you're logged out or logged in as someone else -- or have a friend try the link.

Surprise! The work downloads. It will also download if the creator or the challenge owner, who are both able to see the work and its download links, click the download link.

(The good news is you need to know the title and the creator of the work or have someone give you the download link directly, so it's not super easy.)

*What should happen*
You should get a flash message saying "Sorry, you can't download an unrevealed work" and you should be directed to the /works page. Really! It says so right in the code: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/downloads_controller.rb#L23

*Update 5 November 2017*
On production, it is no longer possible to download an unrevealed work, yay! _However_, even though you're redirected to the /works index, you don't receive an error message, so that's a bit of a problem.

column1: Add comment freezing to all comments
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In order to prevent discussions in work and news post comment threads from getting off-topic and becoming distressful to users, we want to introduce LiveJournal-style comment freezing to the Archive.

The broad specifications for the feature are as follows:

* *Works:* the feature should be available only to work owners and policy_and_abuse and superadmin admins
* *News posts:* the feature should only be available to AO3 admins
* *Tags:* the feature should only be available to tag_wrangling and superadmin admins
* When available, it should add a toggle button with initial text *Freeze Thread* and alternate text *Unfreeze Thread* to each comment in a thread
* When a valid user clicks on *Freeze Thread* on a comment, it should:
*# toggle the button to *Unfreeze Thread*
*# NOT hide any of the comments in the thread
*# hide the *Reply* button
*# prevent anyone from adding a reply to that comment and any child comments (i.e.: back-end check - don't rely only on removing the button)
*# display a message or some clear visual and non-visual indicator on the frozen comment to indicate that the comment thread is frozen
*# apply all of the above to each child comment as well
*# still allow people to reply to parents and ancestors of the frozen comment

* Clicking on *Unfreeze Thread* on a comment should:
*# toggle the button to *Freeze Thread*
*# remove any visual indication that the comment thread is frozen
*# display the *Reply* button
*# allow anyone to reply to the comment and all its children

We suggest starting this work by implementing all the above steps as Cucumber tests, and discussing any design questions in Slack.

16/Jan/21 4:38 PM;5ded904a73b0bd0e4d82dd09;* Availability: 
** As a user, could freeze comments on my own works but not others' works, news posts, or tag pages 
** As a PAC admin, could freeze comments on works and news posts, but not tag pages 
* Freezing:
** Freezing a comment thread refreshed the page (jump to top) and gave the blue flash message “Comment thread successfully frozen\!”; scrolling down showed that the comment and everything downstream was now frozen. 
** In place of the Reply button, a selected Frozen “button” appears; in place of Freeze Thread, I see “Unfreeze Thread”. All other buttons (including spam) look and work as normal. 
** It does not matter what the frozen/unfrozen states of the child comments were, freezing the parent freezes every child comment
** Trying to submit a reply to a frozen comment (due to still having the window open) refreshed the page with the red flash message “Sorry, you cannot reply to a frozen comment.”; scrolling down showed that the comment and everything downstream was now frozen
** Trying to freeze a frozen comment (due to already having frozen it in another tab) gives the red flash message “Sorry, that comment thread could not be frozen.”
* Unfreezing: 
** Unfreezing a comment thread refreshed the page and gave the blue flash message “Comment thread successfully unfrozen\!”; scrolling down showed that the comment and everything downstream was no longer frozen
** Unfreezing a child comment but not its parent only affects that child and its children, as expected. 
** It does not matter what the frozen/unfrozen states of the child comments were, unfreezing the parent unfreezes every child comment 
** Trying to submit a reply to a frozen comment (due to still having the window open) that I then unfroze before hitting submit on my reply worked as normal/no indication that there was ever a frozen comment
** Trying to unfreeze an unfrozen comment (due to already having unfrozen it in another tab) gives the red flash message “Sorry, that comment thread could not be unfrozen.”
* Freezing and spam: 
** I can spam a frozen comment, and it stays frozen.
** I can unspam a frozen spam comment, and it stays frozen. 
** I can freeze a spam comment, but it does not stay spam. 
** I can unfreeze a frozen spam comment, but it does not stay spam. 
** If the spam comment has replies, freezing/unfreezing that comment will freeze/unfreeze the thread as normal, but as stated above, the comment gets unspammed. (If there are spam replies to that comment, those replies stay spam and get frozen/unfrozen as normal, however.)

18/Jan/21 1:09 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3963|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3963|smart-link]  *ready  for testing*

h2. Purpose

* Stops checking comments for spam whenever they are saved. This will allow spam comments to be frozen/unfrozen and prevent errors when you freeze/unfreeze the same comments repeatedly for testing purposes. It will also prevent comments you manually marked as spam from getting reverted by the spam checker.
* Removes the {{cursor: pointer}} CSS style that was being applied to all manner of things. Now we defer to whatever cursor the browser chooses for specific elements. (This will stop the pointer from showing up on "Frozen" and other things with the {{.current}} style, incorrectly making it look clickable. It also means some clickable things like buttons will now have the default arrow cursor, because that's what browsers do for those.)
* Update the redirect when freezing and unfreezing comments. Simply redirecting back would result in the comment section collapsing if you'd loaded comments with AJAX. So now we redirect to all comments, expanded, like when you mark something as ham/spam. AO3-6036 is the existing issue for it not redirecting you to the proper page.

h2. Testing Instructions

* Mark a comment as spam and make sure it doesn't get unmarked as spam when you freeze or unfreeze it.
* Make sure you don't get an error when repeatedly freezing and unfreezing the same comment.
* Make sure the "Frozen" indicator doesn't have the same cursor you see when hovering over a link.
* Make sure you get redirected to the comment's ultimate parent with comments shown when freezing/unfreezing.

column1: Allow admins to bulk search users by email
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
To aid in finding existing authors on AO3 during an import and prevent duplicate imports and irate messages from users, Open Doors admins want to be able to enter a list of email addresses and get back a list of corresponding AO3 accounts.

*API*
See AO3-4741

*UI*
- The existing admin user search page should be extended to take comma-separated values in the existing field OR add a new field to list line break delimited emails (like the import work field). 
- It should return the results in the existing format of the find users page, but also provide a button to download the results as a csv file so Open Doors can populate a Google spreadsheet for manual imports.
column133:
03/Nov/16 4:24 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;After discussion with Open Doors, who will be the main users for this feature, the UI in the Archive should be implemented as follows:
* Add a *Find Users* option in the *Manage Users* menu
* Add a *Bulk Email Search* option in the *Manage Users* menu
* The Find Users form will remain the default page for the admin section
* The *Bulk Email Search* option should load a new page with the following UI elements:
** a large input box
** a submit button
** the same paginated output as the existing *Find Users*
** a *Download as CSV* button
* the input box will allow admins to paste in a line-break separated list of emails (see Work Import form)
* the Submit button will pass this to the backend, where each email will be checked for an _exact_ match in the Users table
* the list of found user accounts will then be displayed as table (see Find Users form)
* the CSV generated should contain only the user's id, login name and email address
column134:
30/Nov/16 1:35 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;This is a pull request purely for the UI part of this ticket: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/2643

The *Bulk Email Search* feature is a new entry in Admin section > *Manage Users*. When you paste a list of line-break separated email addresses into the form and press *Find*, you should see:
- a plain comma-separated list of email addresses that weren't found
- a paginated table of user accounts for all the email addresses on the list that were found (this is the same table that appears when doing a normal search by user or email)
- if you press *Download CSV* instead of *Find*, you will get all of the above and your browser should download an Excel-friendly CSV file containing all the original addresses with their AO3 logins if they have one, or a blank cell in the Login column if they don't

column1: Mobile Chrome thinks pagination links should call us maybe
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In mobile Chrome, go to a /works page for a tag with a lot of works, e.g. Supernatural: http://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Supernatural/works

Use the pagination links to navigate through the pages of works until you notice the pagination buttons taking on a stacked appearance, as shown here:
 !Stacked links.jpeg|thumbnail! 

Using Chrome's back and forward buttons may cause the stack to gain layers -- that is, you might see three or four grey rectangles on top of each other instead of two:
 !More stacked links.jpeg|thumbnail! 

Note that in iOS, if you hold your finger on a link with a stacked appearance, Chrome pops up options for a telephone number or a FaceTime call:
 !Telephone link.jpeg|thumbnail! 
 !Also a horrifically broken link.jpeg|thumbnail!  

*What should happen instead*
The pagination links should not take on this stacked appearance, and they should behave like regular links when you hold your finger on one:
 !Normal link.jpeg|thumbnail! 

(Note how the top of the pop up just displays the URL of the page the link points to.)
column133:
03/Nov/16 5:35 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;There's a meta tag for disabling detection of phone numbers: <meta name="format-detection" content="telephone=no"> (Source: https://developers.google.com/web/fundamentals/native-hardware/click-to-call/)

But it doesn't appear to work correctly in Chrome -- just Safari. For example...

When I have the pagination options 1 2 ... 9 10 11 12 13 14 15 16 17 ... 39 40 at the top of the page, the 9 10 11 12 13 14 15 16 part gets converted into a telephone link by Chrome, creating the display issues shown above. (This behavior does _not_ happen in Safari.)

If I just include the numbers on the page without all the HTML that goes into our pagination, the same numbers also get turned into a telephone link. This behavior is the same in both Safari and Chrome.

When I add the meta tag to the page head, Safari honors it: the numbers are not a telephone link. Chrome ignores it and the numbers remain a link.

I think the pagination issue is a case of "oops, Chrome broke something related to telephone link detection." :|
column134: 03/Nov/16 5:41 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Yeeeeeah, I can recreate this behavior on FanFiction.Net. It's not us. column1: Hits to the most recent chapter of a work should increase the hit count
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Current behavior:*
A multi-chapter work's hit count only increases when someone visits the first chapter of the work. 

This is undesirable because:
1. Subscription notifications contain a link directly to the newly-posted chapter, and visits from those links don't increase the work's hits.
2. People sometimes share links directly to updates, and visits from those links don't increase the work's hits.
3. People want us to add a link to the most recent chapter on the work blurb (AO3-4750), but if we do that with the current code, visits from that link won't increase the work's hits.

*Desired behavior:*
Going _directly_ to the most recent chapter of a multi-chapter work should increase the work's hits. 

"Directly" here means by following a link that's _not_ on the work. Code-wise, we're defining "on the work" as "any page that has '/works/####' in the URL" (where '####' matches the id of the work the chapter belongs to). 

*Things that should be true when testing:*
1. Following the "Chapter #" link in a subscription notice increases the work's hits.
2. Following a link to a chapter that has been posted anywhere on the web increases the work's hits.
3. Pasting/typing the chapter's URL into your browser (and going there) increases the work's hits.
4. Following the recent chapter link (AO3-4750) in the blurb increases the work's hits.
5. Using the Next Chapter link on the work *does not* increase the work's hits.
6. Using the Chapter Index on the work *does not* increase the work's hits.

Additionally, this uses the existing method of increasing hits, which means:
7. The work's hit count *does not* increase if you're logged in as the work creator.
8. The work's hit count *does not* increase if you access the most recent chapter twice in a row (e.g. if you follow the link in the subscription email and then follow a link on Tumblr).

_Important:_ Hits in the _blurb_ are cached for about an hour. Hits on the _work_ update immediately.
 
*Notes*
Do not merge without AO3-4750. These issues should be deployed together following a news post.
column133: 04/Apr/20 12:54 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;When AO3-5905 is implemented, we will have better hit count support for multi-chaptered works, and this change won't be necessary.

column1: Sorting within user or collection filtered results removes fandom filter
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When viewing filtered results for a user or collection, and then sorting, the filter is removed.

Example:
# Go to a user's dashboard and click on one of their fandoms. This shows you the filtered list of the works they have created in that fandom. The title of the page will for example be "1-3 works by ariana_paris in Testing".
# In the right-hand *Sort and filter* bar, select a sort order (for example, "word count"), then click on the *Sort and filter* button.
# Instead of getting the same 3 works, sorted by word count, you see the list of all the user's works sorted by word count. The Fandom filtering is gone.

This also affects collections (and was reported on Yuletide, for instance).

There is anecdotal evidence that this was caused by a very recent change in the code. Users started reporting it to Support in December, and Open Doors reported that they noticed this behaviour when searching for works, but it wasn't happening before November.

We implemented a somewhat hack-y fix for AO3-4795 : https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7a3713ee8d0b552de6274abb428ad5671f497830/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L109

{code:java}
      # This strange dance is because there is an interaction between
      # strong_parameters and dup, without the dance 
      # options[:filter_ids] << tag.id is ignored.
      filter_ids = options[:filter_ids] || []
      filter_ids << tag.id
      options[:filter_ids] = filter_ids
{code}

Following the switch to Rails 4 and the removal of the strong_parameters gem, we want to see if this fix is still needed, or if we can return to the previous version, which was just:

{code:java}
      options[:filter_ids] ||= []
      options[:filter_ids] << tag.id
{code}

I refer to: https://github.com/rails/strong_parameters

2 Compute a Topological Sort of Active Record Models

We are going to work model by model, and the natural order to do that systematically is topological. That is, if post has many comments, first you do Post, and later you do Comment.

column136:
31/Jan/17 5:55 AM;557058:02bc859b-f215-4095-9ec1-174d75faf55d;I'm still not ready to approve this pull request. A visual review of the code shows that the Ruby is well formed. But, as I do with all pull request reviews, I like to run tests against it. My first pass at the tests showed an issue with a no longer supported feature of Elasticsearch query. For that reason I upgrade my copy of Vagrant to use the version of Elasticsearch that is most readily available -- 2.3.4. Elasticsearch is currently at 5.1 (it jumped from 2.4 to 5.0.) But the tests still failed. I looked at more detail at the use of the rollout gem in this pull request. The ApplicationController does a use_new_search? on every requests, which uses a rollout facility to check if the current_user is to use the new ES search. The Cucumber tests seem to always have a nil current_user so that test was not of much help in Cucumber. So, to test the new ES search (and being as I only had ES 2.3.5 on my Vagrant) I temporarily hard-coded the check for `$rollout.active?` to true. 

But the tests still failed. It failed for a seemingly non-ES-upgrade reason ([bookmarkable] is not a valid type) but I resisted the urge to chase that issue down. When I toggled that hard-coded `$rollout.active?` value to false, it failed for the obvious reason of the use use a bad ES query (unknown search element [facets]).

I have four problems with the pull request:
1) Cucumber tests do not appropriately use `$rollout.activate_user(:use_new_search, <current_user_under_test>)`
2) Cucumber tests, hard-coded to use ES 2.3.4 fail for seemingly non-ES reasons
3) I see nothing in the code to support the use of two ES servers: one for 0.90.7 and one for 2.x or 5.1
4) OTW's Vagrant currently has only ES 0.90.7 and arguably needs 2.x or 5.1 as well

Were I do work further on this task, I would want to first create RSpec tests as I looked for and perhaps enhanced the code and then I'd clean up the Cucumber tests.

23/Jan/17 1:58 PM;557058:02bc859b-f215-4095-9ec1-174d75faf55d;The Skin model has an accepts nested attributes for SkinParent(s). Rails makes it easy to update nested attributes with its fields_for helper. The params passed then send the nested relationship such as:

params[:skin][:skin_parents_attributes]{1=>{"position"=>1, "parent_skin_id"=>795}, 3=>{"position"=>32, "parent_skin_id"=>826}}

The problem I've had is that strong_parameters takes offense to the integer values passed in the skin_parents_attributes hash and errors off. There actually was a pull request to fix that issue (https://github.com/rails/strong_parameters/pull/221
) But the pull was closed without being merged with the understanding that "parameter keys arrive as strings when submitted via HTTP requests" The thing is: integers keys are being passed with the cucumber tests for SkinsController features. My hack fix was to put the following in the SkinsController:

  module ActionController
    class Parameters
      def fields_for_style?(object)
        object.is_a?(Hash) && object.all? { |k, v| k.to_s =~ /\A-?\d+\z/ && v.is_a?(Hash) }
      end
    end
  end

I spoke in detail about this with Scott and he'd like to know if you'd like Corgibytes to pursue this further. There is an issue with Strong Parameters but it may only occur for applications still running in Rails 3.2. Next steps for us would be to add a unit test in rails/strong_parameters that proves there is an issue with Rails 3.2 and then create a pull request to that project. 
Were Corgibytes not to continue researching the nested attributes issue. What I'd do is leave that hack code in SkinsController -- until another controller has the same problem. At that point I'd create a module and use the Ruby 2.0 refinements feature and put the open classing in a module and then include that module in ApplicationController.
Note that earlier last week I began having issues with nested attributes and discovered that there was a bug fix in rails/strong_paramters that hadn't been pushed to the published version of that gem.

column1: Collection email receives "Work added" emails when a mod updates a work's accepted, anonymous, or unrevealed status from Manage Items page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h2. Overview:

If a collection owner supplies a collection email and enables the "Send a message to the collection email when a work is added" option for the collection, that email address will incorrectly receive "Work added" emails when the mods update works using the collection's Manage Items page.

You can use the sub collections here: http://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/AO34854/collections

h2. Steps to reproduce: 

h3. *SCENARIO 1:* Updating a single work's Anonymous or Unrevealed status sends many emails it should not
# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Fill in "Collection email" with an email address you have access to
# Check either "This collection is unrevealed" or "This collection is anonymous"
# Check "Send a message to the collection email when a work is added"
# Submit
# Follow "Post to Collection"
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be included)
# Post Without Preview
# The collection email will receive an email with the subject "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" and a body saying "USER posted a new work to your collection, [COLLECTION NAME]: [WORK TITLE]"
# Return to your collection (you can follow the link on the top of the work)
# Repeat steps 8-10 two more times
# Manage Items > Approved
# Uncheck "Unrevealed" or "Anonymous" on a single work
# Submit


h3. *SCENARIO 2:* Modifying a single work's Approved or Rejected status in a collection sends one email it should not
# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Fill in "Collection email" with an email address you have access to
# Check "Send a message to the collection email when a work is added"
# Submit
# Follow "Post to Collection"
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be included)
# Post Without Preview
# The collection email will receive an email with the subject "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" and a body saying "USER posted a new work to your collection, [COLLECTION NAME]: [WORK TITLE]"
# Return to your collection (you can follow the link on the top of the work)
# Manage Items > Approved
# Change the dropdown menu on the work you added from "Approved" to "Rejected"
# Submit

h2. What happens:

In *SCENARIO 1*, the collection email will receive one "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" email for _each work_ on that page -- so in our example, you will receive three emails.

In *SCENARIO 2*, the collection email will receive exactly one "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" email.

h2. What should happen:

No work is being added to the collection, so no "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" email should be sent when the work's Approved, Rejected, Anonymous, or Unrevealed status is updated.

h2. Notes:

It doesn't matter if you're checking or unchecking Unrevealed or Anonymous. Likewise, it doesn't matter whether you're setting the work to Approved or Rejected. The bug happens no matter what.
