column1: Batch tag count updates to speed up posting
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Current when under high load the systems takes a long time to post new works, this is really only apparent when multiple people are posting works which share the same tag.

Currently posting takes a long time as the following query takes around 2 minutes:

UPDATE `tags` SET `taggings_count` = COALESCE(`taggings_count`, 0) + 1 WHERE `tags`.`type` IN ('Rating') AND `tags`.`id` = 11   

So my plan is to remove taggings_count as a field in the db and make it a method with some smart caching.

*Testing notes:*

- Tags with less than 999 uses are small and should not be cached
- Tags with 1,000-39,999 uses are medium and should be cached for a variable period of time (3-40 minutes)
- Tags with 40,000 uses or more are large and should be cached for 30 minutes

You will want to find a tag in each of these categories, and then go to the edit page for that tag (http://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%A/edit) _before_ you post. *Note the number listed in "Taggings Count (#)" in the sidebar.*

Now post the work. 

Then reload the edit page. The "Taggings Count (#)" should change immediately for the small tag, but it should *not* change for the medium and large tags until the caching period (3-40 minutes) is up.

*Also check* that you can access the pages linked in the sidebar on http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings:

- Fandoms by media (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms
- Characters by fandom (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=characters
- Relationships by fandom (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=relationships
- Freeforms by fandom (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=freeforms
- Unsorted Tags (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/unsorted_tags

On each of those pages, make sure you can sort tags by their taggings count. Click the "↓ Taggings" link at the top of the table (between the Canonical and Manage columns) to sort.

28/Mar/17 3:17 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;It's true that the cached value is fine in almost all cases, but I thought there was a bit of a cyclic dependency going on with the first use of a tag. If a brand new fandom tag is listed as having a taggings_count_cache of 0, I believe it won't show up in the wrangling interface, which means that no one will ever view the taggings_count, and so the cached count won't ever get updated (and therefore it'll never have its taggings_count_cache value set to 1 so that it can appear in the wrangling interface, etc.).

I assume that's why works have an after_save hook that calls update_tag_cache for all of the work's tags -- to make sure that the first use of a tag always gets registered, so that it will be included in the in_use filter.

The Edit page refreshes the taggings count, so it forces it to show up in the Fandoms by Media page. But most people aren't wranglers, so they won't be able to visit the Edit page on the tag they just created and make it show up on the Fandoms by Media page. The steps I'm suggesting are this:

1. Bookmark an External Work with a new fandom.
2. Wait a few minutes for all of the background processes to run.
3. Check the Fandoms by Media page to make sure that the new fandom is visible.

02/Apr/17 7:17 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;For a possible fix, I believe it would work to remove the after_save callback on Works and replace it with after_create and after_destroy callbacks on Taggings. That way it could cover everything that has a tagging: Works, ExternalWorks, and Bookmarks. (As well as any other objects that might potentially end up in the Taggings table in the future, too.)

It might also be a little more efficient, since it would only call update_tag_cache when a tagging is created or destroyed (when the count might need updating), instead of every time a work with that tag is saved (which could trigger recounts/updates even when fixing a typo, with no changes to the tags).

I can put together a pull request if this sounds like a useful change to make.

column1: Unused code in TagSetNominationsController: 404 raised instead of flash error
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There are currently 3 places in TagSetNominationsController that expect to take in an id parameter and find an active record:
# TagSetNominationsController.load_tag_set:22
# TagSetNominationsController.load_nomination:30
# TagSetNominationsController#index:82

If an active record is not found with that id, an ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound error is raised and the user sees a 404 page. The code has an unused path that states if TagSetNomination.find(id) or OwnedTagSet.find(id) returns falsey, return a flash error message. Because the find method can only return an active record or raise an error, this conditional case is never reached.

Possible solutions:
# Don't raise an ActiveRecord error (i.e. use find_by_id) or catch the error, so that the currently unreachable code becomes reachable. Write tests.
# Remove the unreachable code. Write tests.

This came up during AO3-4830 PR review (https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/2728/files#r102482816). Creating a separate JIRA issue to keep this code separate.

column1: Works imported for a previously claimed email address do not transfer if the ao3 account email has changed
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
If the email address on an imported work matches the email address on an ao3 account, works automatically transfer and a notification is sent. If there is no match, an external author identity is created and a claim email is sent. If the works are then claimed, the external author identity records the account they were claimed by. I would expect that works imported for this email address later should transfer to that ao3 account as for matching email address.

However, if the creator has changed their account email from the import email, the works instead appear to be directly on the archivist account with no archivist byline, and a new claim email is sent to the import email address with ALL works attached to that address (including previously claimed ones). The works still all appear under the external author identity. 

We have an occurrence of this happening with the yuletide import, so it's not recent. I was able to replicate this on test: http://test.archiveofourown.org/opendoors/external_authors/2032
column133:

- does the external author’s email match an existing user’s? if so, claim!
- if not, send the email an invitation to join the Archive
I think the missing step there is “does this email address belong to an external author which is already claimed by a user account with a different email” (which is the case here)

column1: Set RuboCop's target Ruby version for Hound
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
By default, RuboCop looks at the .ruby-version file at the project root, if any.

https://github.com/bbatsov/rubocop/blob/3d63895ea625312a8a18303f7343a19075299813/manual/configuration.md#setting-the-target-ruby-version

However, Hound only has access to the changed files in each run.

https://github.com/houndci/hound/issues/1230

So if we want Hound to stop hounding us about Ruby 2.3 features (e.g. https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/2786#discussion_r104586828) we have to set the Ruby version explicitly in .rubocop.yml.

{code}

column1: "Invited" membership level in collections has no purpose
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In collections, there are two ways to join:
1) The collection mods can add you, and assign the permission level they want
2) You can select the "Join" button on a moderated collection, which grants you "None" permission level until the moderators change it to "Member"

There is a permission level "Invited" but it doesn't seem to convey any permissions and is essentially the same as "None". It's possible this was intended for collection owners to invite people, they sit at this level until they accept, but this isn't currently coded. Once a person has been added as a member or below, the "Join" button on the collection's page becomes "Leave". If they’re added as a moderator owner, the button becomes “Membership”.

One of the options for resolving this bug is to simply remove the {{invited}} membership level.

column1: Unapproved/rejected/invited works in an unrevealed/anonymous and moderated collection don't get revealed/de-anoned when the moderator deselects the unrevealed/anonymous collection settings
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Steps to reproduce*
1. Log in as USER1, who will be our collection moderator
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in "Collection name"
4. Fill in "Display title"
5. Check "This collection is moderated"
6. Check "This collection is unrevealed"
7. Press "Submit"
8. Log out as USER1
9. Log in as USER2, who will be our creator
10. If necessary, return to the collection you created as USER1
11. Follow "Post to Collection" link
12. Fill in required information
13. Press "Post Without Preview"
14. Log out as USER2
15. Log in as USER1
16. If necessary, return to the collection you created as USER1
17. Follow "Collection Settings" link in sidebar
18. Uncheck "This collection is unrevealed"
19. Press "Update"

Note: The above is an example. This applies in more cases, as discussed below.

*What should happen*
I'd expect the work to be revealed.

*What happens instead*
The work is not revealed. It still appears under "Awaiting Approval" on the "Manage Items" page and pressing the "Details" button shows a work blurb that says "Part of" without listing the collection name; additionally, the work itself displays a banner that says "This work is part of an ongoing challenge and will be revealed soon\! You can find details here:" without listing the collection name.

Because the "This collection is unrevealed" setting has been de-selected, the "Manage Items" page does not contain an option to reveal the work manually. The good news is if you turn "This collection is unrevealed" on and then off again, the work will be revealed and all will be right in the world.

*Notes*
This issue previously mentioned problems with unchecking the “This collection is moderated” setting; however, they are separate issues and should be handled separately… if the issues with moderated collections were still happening, but they are not. (Previously, if a moderator unchecked “This collection is moderated” while works were awaiting approval, the work count in the sidebar would increase but the works would not appear in the collection. Now the count does not increase.)

*Testing notes*
All works regardless of approval status should be revealed or de-anoned upon unchecking the relevant collection setting. 

*In the case of invited works in an unrevealed collection*, only works that have been approved by the work creator should have gift, prompt fill, or related work notifications sent. (Notifications are only sent for these works because they are the only works that will appear unrevealed. It’s not possible to invite a work to an unrevealed collection, but if a collection moderator invites a work to a collection and _then_ sets the collection to unrevealed while waiting for the creator’s approval‌_,_ the work will not be unrevealed.)

If both the collection moderator and work creator have approved the work’s inclusion in the collection, the gift and prompt fill notifications should include the name of the collection.

*If you’re testing with the anonymous setting* rather than the unrevealed setting, note that de-anoning does not send gift, prompt fill, or related work notifications – it sends subscription notifications if you are subscribed to a creator whose work was de-anoned.

There are a couple of issues that might come up in testing that are existing bugs:

* If a work is in both Regular Collection and Unrevealed Collection, the notification emails that are sent when Unrevealed Collection is revealed _might_ say "A gift work has been posted for you in the Regular Collection collection." That's because the emails only list the work's _first_ collection.
* If the moderator reveals the collection, sets it back to unrevealed, and then reveals it again, a second set of notifications will be sent.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Trying to leave a comment on a work, or post a work, generates a 502 error if the comment /work/author's notes includes an angled bracket under the following circumstances:

abc <
xyz

and

abc<
xyz

The angled bracket must be at the end of a line of text, with nothing after it on that line, but with more text on a subsequent line, to trigger the 502 error.  

Other placements of the angled bracket don't cause this error:

abc < xyz (comes through correctly)

abc<xyz (cuts off everything from the angled bracket on)

abc <xyz (cuts off everything from the angled bracket on)

<abc (triggers a "Content can't be blank" message)

abc <3 xyz (comes through correctly)

abc <3

column1: Synonyms and canonicals do not take and works do not show
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Different wranglers have reported encountering these issues since the 29th of March.

Normally, after synning a tag in the edit page (by adding an existing canonical tag in the "Synonym of" box and saving, the fandom of the canonical tag will be attached automatically in the "Fandoms" box. After 1-10 minutes the works will show at the works page e.g. ([edit page|http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Sassy%20Castiel/edit]) ([work page|http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Sassy%20Castiel/works]). Works would also show after canonising tags by ticking the "Canonical" box.

Occasionally we will encounter issues especially during high archive usage times. But for the most parts, everything takes after a few minutes.

However, for the past couple of weeks, works have repeatedly not show nor does the fandoms get attached. It takes many tries (manually desynning then resynning, or decanonising then recanonising) to get works to show, even during archive low usage periods. A staff also reported issues during staff allocated days (Wed/Fri). 

For syns with more than one work, there are some cases where only some of the works show but others don't. Reindexing the works does not fix the problem.
column133:
26/Apr/20 7:06 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This issue is basically the same as [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|smart-link] , except that it specifically seems to have gotten much worse after the taggings count changes in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4858|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4858|smart-link].

I think the reason it got worse was because the taggings count is displayed on the tag edit page. When the taggings count for a small tag is displayed, it’s recalculated and cached, and queued for writing to the database in batches. This happens even if the taggings count hasn’t changed.

This means that very soon after viewing the tag edit page – that is, soon after visiting the page you need to visit in order to make a tag canonical or add a synonym – the tag is updated in a batch transaction that might cause any other transactions involving that tag to be very slow. I believe that [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|smart-link] is caused by jobs being queued before the end of the transaction. The competition between the batch update and the canonical/synonym update probably caused even longer delays between when the job was queued (in the {{before_update}} callback) and when the data was committed to the database.

Hopefully resolving [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|smart-link] should be sufficient to fix this even without updating the taggings count code to reduce the number of updates.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
First, you'll need a canonical tag that uses an ampersand. You can use [Character A & Character B|http://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Character%20A%20*a*%20Character%20B] on staging, or make a new one by doing the following:

1. Log in with an account with tag wrangling privileges
2. Browse > Tags > New Tag
3. Fill in the desired tag name in "Name," e.g. Character A & Character B
4. Check the "Canonical" checkbox
5. Select a Category
6. Press "Create Tag"

There are certain autocomplete fields where -- once you begin typing the tag name -- the tag will show up in the autocomplete dropdown list not as Character A & Character B, but instead as Character A &; Character B, with a semicolon after the ampersand (screenshot1). After you select the tag from the dropdown, it will appear correctly on the form, without the semicolon (screenshot2).

The bug doesn't _always_ happen immediately. If it doesn't, try either (a) typing more of the tag name, or (b) selecting the tag from the dropdown, using the × to remove it, and then typing the tag name into the autocomplete field again. 

I've had the most luck reproducing it by typing everything up to and including the space _after_ the & sign (e.g. typing "Character A & " for a relationship or "Pete & " for a fandom), but I'm not 100% ready to say that's the cause of the bug.

This bug does _not_ appear to happen on:
- the work posting form (http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/new). 

It does appear to happen on:
- the tag set form (http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/new)

column1: Regular users see cached admin pages, admins see cached regular pages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
1. Log in as an admin
2. Go to Admin Posts > Archive FAQ
3. Leave the admin FAQ page open
4. Open another browser or incognito/private window and _don't_ log in as an admin
5. Go to About > FAQ

Surprise! The non-admin will find themselves looking at the admin FAQ page: it will have the teal admin navigation, the Admin | Log Out options in the upper corner, and everything else an admin should see and a regular user should not. This all _seems_ to be easier to reproduce with a logged out user than a logged in one, but it does happen for logged in users as well. 

The opposite happens, too, and it's not just the FAQ page.

1. Logged out, or logged in as a regular user, go to the languages page: http://test.ao3.org/languages
2. Open another browser or incognito/private window and log in as admin
3. Go to the languages page: http://test.ao3.org/languages

The admin will see the non-admin version of the page: no teal navigation, no indication that they are logged in as an admin. (It's tricky to reproduce this after you've already done the steps to make a regular user see the admin pages, but it can happen. You'll have better luck if you log out in both browsers and wait a few minutes.) 

The good news is the non-admin can't actually _do_ anything they're no supposed to, since it appears they're just getting a cached page, but this is still Not Good.

The easiest way to test this is to log in as an admin and then check that you have a cookie called admin_credentials.
- Instructions for checking for specific cookies in Chrome: http://www.wikihow.com/View-Cookies#Google_Chrome_sub
- Instructions for checking for specific cookies in Safari: http://www.loopinsight.com/2015/08/06/how-to-view-safari-cookies/

column1: Deleting a bookmark redirects to first page of bookmarks, even when bookmark was on a different page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When viewing account's bookmarks list and deleting a bookmark from any page after page 1, user is redirected to page 1 after bookmark is deleted. This makes it difficult to keep track of one's place in the list when deleting bookmarks from later pages. This also resets all the search filters the user set, which makes it even more difficult to keep track.

Work-around has been to open the "delete" link in a different tab or window so that original tab/window remains on the correct page.

h2. Testing instructions

This issue was expanded to generally apply to pages that list bookmarks, not just the account’s bookmarks list. So these testing instructions have been updated from the Jira comment from Danaël Villeneuve.

After bookmarking, you may have to wait 5-10 minutes each for the bookmark to appear in listings. (Javascript needs to be enabled for these testing steps.)

# Log in
# Bookmark a work that is in at least one canonical tag (e.g. it’s in a canonical fandom)
# Follow the link to that canonical tag on the work blurb
# Follow “Bookmarks”
# Filter the list in some way that includes your bookmark but excludes some other bookmarks
# Press “Delete” on your bookmark
# You should stay on the same filtered page
# Bookmark a series
# Navigate to that series
# Follow the bookmarks link on the series
# Press “Delete” on your bookmark
# You should say on the series' bookmarks page
# Bookmark a work. Add this bookmark to a collection that already contains some bookmarks
# Go to the collection’s bookmarked items page
# Filter the list in some way that includes your bookmark but excludes some other bookmarks
# Press “Delete” on your bookmark
# You should stay on the same filtered page
# Bookmark a work
# Navigate to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search]
# Fill “Bookmarker” with your own username
# Press “Search Bookmarks”
# Press “Delete” on one of your bookmarks
# You should stay on the same filtered page
# Bookmark two works and add a bookmarker’s note for only one of the bookmarks
# Hi, username! > My Bookmarks
# Filter the list to only include bookmarks with notes
# Press “Delete” on one of your bookmarks
# You should stay on the same filtered page

column1: Chapter: Make it easier to see and add co-authors who are already on the work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. The Background

Strong parameters broke the bug that was causing AO3-3752: "Adding a co-author to any chapter of a work will cause them to be an author on all subsequently posted chapters whether you like it or not" \o/

So, yay, co-authors are no longer added to subsequently posted chapters whether you like it or not.

However, now we need to clean up the broken code, add some tests, and implement the design from that issue.


h1. The Issue

!3752.png|thumbnail! 

There should be handy checkboxes so you can add co-creators who are already on the work to a chapter. This is the shiny new "Chapter co-creators" area. It should be available when creating or editing a chapter on a co-authored work.

Once a given co-creator is added to a chapter, their checkbox will be disabled and you will not be able to remove them.

If there are no co-creators already on the work, there should be no "Chapter co-creators" section.

On the chapter form, where it used to say "Current co-creators," it now says "Work co-creators" to distinguish them from chapter co-creators. The work form should say "Current co-creators."

The other change is everything on the form (for chapters and works) now says "creator" instead of "author."

h1. Testing Notes

This might be more confusing than clicking around and checking the page against the description above, but if you want step by step instructions for checking out what's on the chapter form, try this:

1. Log in
2. Post > New Work
3. Fill in the required information
4. Post Without Preview
5. Add Chapter
6. Under "Chapter Preface," notice that there are no "Work co-creators" or "Chapter co-creators" sections
7. Check "Add co-creator?" 
8. Fill in the field with another user's name, e.g. "testy2"
9. Fill in some chapter text
10. Post Without Preview
11. Notice that the chapter and the work now have two authors listed
12. Edit Chapter
13. Under "Chapter Preface," notice that there are "Work co-creators" and "Chapter co-creators" sections, that the information in them is correct, and that the checkbox for your co-creator (e.g. testy2) in the "Chapter co-creator" is checked and disabled
14. Return to the work
15. Add Chapter
16. Under "Chapter Preface" and "Chapter co-creators," notice that the checkbox for your co-author (e.g. testy2) is unchecked -- leave it that way
17. Fill in some chapter text
18. Post Without Preview
19. Notice that the chapter you've posted has a byline just says "by [your user name]"
20. Edit Chapter
21. Under "Chapter Preface" and "Chapter co-creators," notice that the checkbox for your co-author (e.g. testy2) is still unchecked -- leave it that way
22. Check "Add co-creators?" 
23. Fill in the field with a third user's name, e.g. "testy4" (don't use testy3 unless AO3-4998 is fixed)
24. Fill in some chapter text
25. Post Without Preview
26. Notice the chapter now has a byline that says "by [your user name], [user name of the third user]" and the work byline now includes all three users
27. Previous Chapter
28. Edit Chapter
29. Under "Chapter Preface," notice that there are "Work co-creators" and "Chapter co-creators" sections, that the information in them is correct, and that the checkbox for your co-creator on this chapter (e.g. testy2) in the "Chapter co-creator" is checked and disabled, but the checkbox for your third co-creator (e.g. testy4) is unchecked

column1: Child comments of spam comments should not disappear
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
From LadyOscar's comment on [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-177#icft=AO3-177|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-177#icft=AO3-177|smart-link]:

{quote}1) If a comment marked as spam has children, they will become invisible to anyone but admins along with the spam comment. (When viewed as admin, they have a "Spam" button rather than "Not Spam", so they're presumably not being marked as spam.) They are still included in the overall comment count.

2) Deleting the parent marked as spam causes the child comment to re-appear, with "(Previous comment deleted.)" as a placeholder parent. The comment count is now correct for the number of visible comments.

It seems undesirable for someone's non-spam response to be automatically hidden when a comment is hidden as spam; if the response is considered irrelevant or confusing (by the work creator, comment leaver, or admin) with the spam gone, it can always be deleted.{quote}

It’s also important to ensure spam comments without non-spam replies are _not_ counted toward pagination (formerly [AO3-6008|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6088]):

# Log in
# Post a work (but this mainly happens on news posts)
# Leave a comment on the work
# Log out
# Leave 26 more comments on the work (top level, not threaded)
# Reply to the 25th comment (i.e., not the last comment, but the one before it) 
# Log in as the work creator
# Go to the comment section with all the spam
# Mark all but the first and last +top-level+ comments as spam (i.e., don’t mark the reply from step 6 as spam)

Currently, there are still two pages of comments, but each page only displays one comment.

But there _should_ be one page with three comments and a placeholder, because

* the spam comments should not count toward pagination, and
* the spam comment with the non-spam reply should display as a placeholder with a visible reply

Altering the Post New Work form's source, either manually or with a translation tool, will allow you to create tags.

One way to reproduce, using Safari for the specifics:
1. Log in

2. Post > New Work

3. In a browser with developer tools enabled, choose Show Web Inspector from Develop
menu (or your browser's equivalent) or right-click the field you want to modify and
choose Inspect Element, e.g. Rating.

4. Locate the select menu, which looks something like this: 
<select id="work_rating_string" name="work\[rating_string]">
<option value="Not Rated" selected="selected">Not Rated</option>
<option value="General Audiences">General Audiences</option>
<option value="Teen And Up Audiences">Teen And Up Audiences</option>
<option value="Mature">Mature</option>
<option value="Explicit">Explicit</option>
</select>

5. In the Web Inspector, right click on the part that says <select id="work_rating_string"
name="work\[rating_string]"> and choose Edit as HTML.

6. Modify the select field by adding an option and removing the selected attribute
of the current rating, e.g.
<select id="work_rating_string" name="work\[rating_string]">
<option value="Made Up Rating">Made Up Rating</option>
<option value="Not Rated">Not Rated</option>
<option value="General Audiences">General Audiences</option>
<option value="Teen And Up Audiences">Teen And Up Audiences</option>
<option value="Mature">Mature</option>
<option value="Explicit">Explicit</option>
</select>

7. Fill in the necessary information to create a work and post.

8. See your work has been successfully created with your made up warning, category,
or rating, like on [http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1064520,|http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1064520,] which has the non-canonical rating "PWP Smutty Smut," the non-canonical category "ALL THE CATEGORIES ALL THE PORN," and the non-canonical warning "IT HAS WAY TOO MUCH SEX RUN FOR YOUR LIFE."

A brief history of this bug may be found in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2728#icft=AO3-2728|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2728#icft=AO3-2728|smart-link] and AO3-3724. 

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4275#icft=AO3-4275|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4275#icft=AO3-4275|smart-link] has been created for cleaning up existing non-canonical tags.

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

It should not be possible to add warnings, categories, or ratings. 

If you use a noncanonical rating, it should fail with the error about required tags being missing.

 If you use a single noncanonical warning, it should fail with an error message about required warning tags being missing.

If you use a noncanonical warning _and_ a canonical one, it should just silently fail to add the noncanonical.

If you use a noncanonical category, it should silently fail to add it.
